The monarch, who rarely makes political statements, stressed the need for Spain to “maintain good neighbourly relations” with Rabat after an unprecedented migrant surge into Ceuta in July strained historically delicate ties.  

The remarks were reported by FRANCE 24’s Sarah Morris from Madrid.
summary: King Felipe VI said Ceuta and Melilla were an inalienable part of Spain during a landmark visit to the north African territories claimed by Morocco. He emphasized Spain's need to maintain good neighbourly relations with Rabat after July's unprecedented migrant surge into Ceuta strained historically delicate ties.
author: France 24

title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi Aramco facilities and say more strikes will follow
content:
Yemen’s Iran‑backed Houthis said on Wednesday that they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco. The claim followed Saudi officials’ report of a strike on a building in an area that houses the energy company’s operations centre.

Powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital, Riyadh, as the coalition fighting the Houthis announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the group toward the city.

The Houthis said the attack was part of a broader campaign and vowed to carry out more attacks.
summary: Yemen's Houthis said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant's operations centre. Powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital, and the coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a missile fired by the Iran‑backed group toward Riyadh.
author: France 24

title: Phoenix youth activists of Turning Point USA rally to honor Charlie Kirk ahead of midterms
content:
Young ultra‑conservatives in Phoenix are mobilizing to preserve the legacy of far‑right influencer Charlie Kirk, who was assassinated in September 2025. The activists, members of Turning Point USA—the organization Kirk co‑founded—are focusing their efforts on energizing the youth electorate ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

More than a year after Kirk’s death, the group says it is working “tirelessly” to honor his memory by organizing rallies, canvassing, and voter‑registration drives aimed at young voters. Their goal is to translate Kirk’s influence into electoral support for conservative candidates in the forthcoming midterms.
summary: More than a year after the September 2025 assassination of far‑right influencer Charlie Kirk, young activists from Turning Point USA are active in Phoenix. They are working to honour his legacy by rallying the youth vote ahead of the US midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Houthis say they hit Aramco facilities and threaten more Saudi attacks
content:
Yemen's Houthi rebels announced on Wednesday that they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco following a strike reported by officials in Riyadh on a building located in the area that houses the energy company's headquarters.

The Iran‑backed militia also claimed to have launched missile strikes on the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and said the attacks were part of a broader campaign against the kingdom.

The Houthis vowed to continue striking Saudi airports and oil facilities, indicating an intent to further escalate their operations.
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco after Riyadh officials reported a strike on a building in the area housing the company's headquarters. The Iran-back militia also claimed missile strikes on Riyadh and vowed to continue attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities.
author: France 24

title: Fact check: Viral graph on Russian data‑center attacks and AfD bot activity is misleading
content:
A fact‑check has examined a viral graph that suggested attacks on Russian data centers led to a decline in bot activity surrounding Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. The graphic was widely shared as evidence of a causal link between the cyber‑attacks and reduced online manipulation.

The review found the graph to contain significant inconsistencies and noted that it offers no supporting evidence for the claimed reduction in bot activity. Consequently, the claim that the attacks diminished Russian‑linked bot operations around the AfD is unsubstantiated.
summary: A viral graph claimed that attacks on Russian data centers reduced bot activity around Germany's AfD. The fact check found significant inconsistencies in the graph and no evidence supporting the claim.
author: DW World

title: Climate change and drone attacks worsen Sudan's humanitarian crisis, health system at risk
content:
Climate change and drone attacks are worsening an already severe humanitarian crisis in war‑torn Sudan, according to the headline.

Aid groups have warned that the country’s health system faces an imminent collapse as fighting continues to displace civilians during the planting season.

The United Nations has responded by extending an arms embargo, but the measure applies only to the Darfur region.
summary: Aid groups say the health system in Sudan could collapse as fighting displaces civilians during the planting season. The United Nations has extended an arms embargo limited to Darfur.
author: DW World

title: Riot police deployed in Tirana as students protest after fire at Education Ministry
content:
A fire broke out at Albania’s Education Ministry in the capital Tirana as students staged protests, according to reports.

Riot police were deployed in Tirana on the second day of the demonstrations, and the sudden outbreak was noted as reminiscent of the widespread protests in France that have attracted international attention.
summary: Riot police were deployed in Tirana on the second day of student protests. The protests, sparked by a fire at the Education Ministry, were compared to recent demonstrations in France.
author: DW World

title: India urges Russia and Ukraine to ensure safe Black Sea commercial shipping
content: New Delhi has called on both Moscow and Kyiv to guarantee the safety of commercial vessels operating in the Black Sea. The Indian government said the request comes as recent attacks in the region have placed Indian seafarers at risk.
summary: New Delhi wants Moscow and Kyiv to ensure safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea. The request comes amid attacks that put Indian seafarers at risk.
author: DW World

title: WHO urges urgent health action in Eastern Mediterranean
content:
The head of the World Health Organization has urged immediate action to promote, provide and protect health across the Eastern Mediterranean region. The call comes as the area faces some of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises.

The WHO chief highlighted Sudan, Yemen and the Occupied Palestinian Territory as key locations where urgent health measures are needed.
summary: The head of the World Health Organization called for promoting, providing and protecting health in the Eastern Mediterranean region. The region includes major humanitarian crises such as Sudan, Yemen and the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
author: UN News

title: WFP warns humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen as fighting blocks aid to 800,000
content:
The United Nations World Food Programme warned on Wednesday that intensifying fighting in Yemen could trigger a humanitarian catastrophe as aid deliveries are increasingly blocked.  

The agency said the conflict has cut off life‑saving assistance for 800,000 people, with shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restricting access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones.
summary: The UN World Food Programme said intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life‑saving assistance to 800,000 people. Shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity have severely restricted access to Taiz and other conflict zones.
author: UN News

title: Guinea-Bissau health minister denies approval of Danish hepatitis B newborn trial
content:
Guinea‑Bissau’s health minister said on Tuesday that the government has not authorized a Danish‑led hepatitis B trial in newborns, refuting claims that the country approved the controversial study.

The proposed research, which would be funded by the United States government and private partners, has been promoted by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., identified in the report as the secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and a longtime anti‑vaccine activist.

According to the minister, the trial would not examine vaccine safety or effectiveness; instead it would monitor “nonspecific” health outcomes such as overall mortality and neurodevelopmental conditions.
summary: Guinea-Bissau's health minister said the government did not authorize the Danish-led hepatitis B trial in newborns. The study, funded by the US government and private partners, would track nonspecific health outcomes such as overall mortality and neurodevelopmental conditions rather than vaccine safety or effectiveness.
author: Guardian World

title: Three Saudi Pro League matches postponed after Houthi attacks, including Al Nassr
content:
The Saudi Pro League announced the postponement of three matches after Houthi attacks, one of which involves Al Nassr, the club of Cristiano Ronaldo.  

The league’s decision affects the scheduled fixtures for the three affected teams, with Al Nassr’s game among those delayed.
summary: The Saudi Pro League postponed three games following Houthi attacks. One of the delayed matches involves Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr side.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN urges Israel to increase actions against settler violence
content:
The United Nations has called on Israel to take additional measures to stop settler violence, according to a report in Jerusalem Daily.  

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned again that Israel’s “enemies” are planning an attack before the upcoming elections.  

Both the UN demand and Netanyahu’s warning were highlighted in the Jerusalem Daily article.
summary: The UN has demanded that Israel do more to stop settler violence. Netanyahu warned again that Israel’s ‘enemies’ are planning an attack before elections.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN official warns food crisis if Hormuz fertiliser plan stalls
content:
A United Nations official warned that a looming food crisis could arise as the plan to move fertiliser through the Hormuz Strait stalls.  

The official said that without a quick deal to transport fertiliser through the strait, agricultural productivity would “significantly drop.”
summary: A UN official warned that a stalled fertiliser plan through the Hormuz Strait could lead to a looming food crisis. The official said agricultural productivity would "significantly drop" without a quick deal to move fertiliser through the strait.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Social Security benefits to increase 3.6% in 2027
content:
US Social Security benefits are set to rise by 3.6 percent in 2027, according to the announcement.  

The increase will add roughly $75 to the monthly checks received by retired Americans, a boost that comes as many face widespread inflation challenges.
summary: Benefits will rise by 3.6 percent in 2027. Retired Americans will receive about $75 more per month.
author: Al Jazeera

title: At least two security officials killed near Iran's critical Chabahar port
content:
At least two security officials were killed in an incident near Iran’s strategic Chabahar port, according to Iranian authorities.  

Iran said the attack was carried out by “terrorist groups” that receive support from outside the country and are targeting the nation’s security forces.
summary: At least two security officials were killed near Iran's critical Chabahar port. Iran says 'terrorist groups' supported from outside the country are targeting security forces.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tehran municipality accused of overstep after launching welfare projects
content:
Tehran’s municipal government has launched a series of new welfare projects, prompting accusations that the initiative represents an “overstep” by the city’s authorities.  

Critics have focused on the projects’ funding sources, questioned their transparency, and raised concerns that they may contribute to inflation.
summary: The Tehran municipality has been accused of overstepping after launching new welfare projects. The projects have faced intense criticism over funding sources, transparency and inflation claims.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Albania experiments with artificial intelligence in politics
content:
Albania is experimenting with artificial intelligence in politics, a development highlighted in a recent analysis titled “AI in politics: Is Albania the EU’s testing ground?”  

The country's foray into AI-driven political applications marks a notable shift toward integrating advanced technology within its governance framework.  

The article’s title raises the question of whether Albania is being used as a testing ground for the European Union’s broader AI initiatives.
summary: Albania is experimenting with artificial intelligence in politics. The experiment focuses on political applications.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan arrested by FBI after more than a year at company
content:
A Saudi engineer at OpenAI, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was taken into custody by the FBI, a case that has been described in reports with references to “toilet paper and secret recorders.”  

Alfozan had been employed by the AI company for more than a year before the arrest. The FBI’s action marks the latest development in the investigation of the OpenAI employee.
summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi engineer, worked for OpenAI for more than a year. He was arrested by the FBI.
author: BBC World

title: Australia’s first Michelin stars awarded to 11 South Australian restaurants
content:
Australia’s inaugural Michelin stars have been awarded to 11 restaurants, all located in South Australia.  

The concentration of the awards in a single state follows reports that the South Australian government financed incognito inspectors to assess the venues.  

These 11 establishments thus become the first Australian restaurants to receive Michelin recognition.
summary: Australia’s first-ever Michelin stars were awarded to 11 restaurants. All of the restaurants are in South Australia, reportedly because the state government paid for incognito inspectors to visit.
author: BBC World

title: US inflation climbs to 3.7% in year to September, driven by motor fuel costs
content: U.S. inflation accelerated to an annual rate of 3.7% for the year ending in September, outpacing expectations. The increase was largely driven by higher motor fuel costs, which lifted overall price growth. The rise signals a broader upward pressure on consumer prices across the United States.
summary: The pace of price rises increased to 3.7% in the year to September. The increase was driven by higher motor fuel costs.
author: BBC World

title: Selma Blair charged with two counts of assault after plane incident
content: Selma Blair, known for her role in Legally Blonde, is facing two counts of assault following an incident on a flight. The charges stem from allegations that she kicked a police officer and a nurse after previously attacking flight attendants during the journey.
summary: The Legally Blonde actress faces two counts of assault for allegedly kicking a police officer and a nurse. These charges follow an alleged attack on attendants during a flight.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Russell T Davies criticises BBC boss's 'clumsy' AI Doctor Who comments
content: BBC director general Matt Brittin has drawn criticism from Russell T Davies after stating he had watched a "pretty good" AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. Davies described Brittin’s remarks on the use of artificial intelligence in the production of the series as "clumsy."
summary: BBC director general Matt Brittin said he had seen a "pretty good" AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. Russell T Davies criticised the director general's comments as clumsy.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Davina McCall says post‑brain surgery memory loss felt like advanced Alzheimer’s
content:
Davina McCall has said that the memory loss she experienced after brain surgery felt like “advanced Alzheimer’s.”  

The TV presenter revealed that she underwent an operation to remove a benign tumour.  

She reported that following the procedure she suffered memory loss.
summary: TV presenter Davina McCall said she suffered memory loss after an operation to remove a benign tumour. She described the loss as feeling like advanced Alzheimer’s.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Shakhtar Donetsk sets up London base for Champions League away from Ukraine
content:
Shakhtar Donetsk, managed by Arda Turan, are based in London for their Champions League campaign, with Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge set to host their home matches as the club lacks a home ground in Ukraine. The team’s statement, “We’re here to show the world that we are alive,” underscores their determination to continue competing despite the ongoing conflict.

In a separate report from their temporary base in Ukraine, the club maintains a spa hotel facility 15 minutes outside Lviv. During a training session, manager Arda Turan and director of football Darijo Srna were observed interacting with players, with Srna demonstrating a skillful shot that prompted Turan to exclaim, “Modric!” This light training was reserved for players who did not start the previous day’s match against Veres Rivne.

The presence of the team in Ukraine remains subject to security risks, as air raid sirens disrupted their peace around dawn at the Lviv base. Similarly, during the match in Rivne, located three hours to the north-east, an alarm forced players and staff into a stadium shelter, delaying the second half by 20 minutes.
summary: Shakhtar Donetsk has established a base in London to host their Champions League matches, with Chelsea's Stamford Bridge serving as their venue. The team continues to face security threats from Russian attacks while training in Ukraine, where air raid sirens regularly disrupt their daily routines.
author: Guardian Sport

title: David Silva to end retirement for one match with Hong Kong club Supreme Sha Tin
content:
Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva is set to make a brief return to professional football at the age of 40, agreeing to play a single match for Supreme Sha Tin. The former international will join a roster of notable players who have previously competed in the territory, including George Best, Bobby Moore, and Diego Forlán.

Hong Kong’s local Premier League has recently sought to elevate its profile, following years of attempts to maintain an independent football association while navigating its status as a special administrative region of China. Although efforts to place a local team in the Chinese Super League during a period of high spending did not materialize, the local league has continued to attract high-profile talent.

Silva’s appearance marks the latest addition to a long history of football in the city, which began during its time as a British colony and has persisted since 1997. The match offers the ambitious club a one-day opportunity to feature a former Premier League star on their team.
summary: Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva is coming out of retirement at age 40 to play a single match for the Hong Kong club Supreme Sha Tin. The article notes that Silva will join a long list of former international stars who have played in the territory.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sunderland to face Torreense in Portugal after 53 years away from Europe
content:
Sunderland prepares to travel to Portugal on Thursday night to face Torreense in the Europa League, marking the club’s first competitive appearance on European soil in 53 years. The visit offers a symbolic parallel to the Black Cats’ last European outing, which was a second leg of a European Cup Winners’ Cup tie against Sporting in Lisbon. That previous encounter occurred when Sunderland were FA Cup holders competing in the Second Division.

Torreense, also a second-tier side, has generated surprise by securing a spot in the Europa League’s initial phase after defeating Sporting in the Portuguese Cup final last season. The Portuguese club’s campaign was further strengthened last month when they recorded a 2-1 victory over Lillestrom in Norway, boosting their prospects for advancing to next spring’s sudden-death rounds. This match provides Sunderland with a respite from a difficult start to their Premier League season.
summary: Sunderland will play Torreense in the Europa League, marking the club's first competitive European match in 53 years. The Black Cats are using this trip as a break from their difficult start to the Premier League season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: New biography details Renée Richards' 1977 US Open lawsuit and current stance
content:
In 1977, ophthalmologist Dr. Renée Richards sued for the right to compete in the women’s draw of the US Open following a sex-change operation. At the time, Richards had excelled as a male amateur player, and her legal battle dominated tennis headlines. The case was successfully argued by the firm of Roy Cohn, who is better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump.

A new biography titled Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman explores this complex legacy. The book details the narrative of Richards’s 1977 lawsuit and highlights her current stance, as she now supports bans on trans athletes in women’s sports.
summary: A new biography by Julie Kliegman explores the complex legacy of tennis pioneer Renée Richards. The book covers her 1977 lawsuit to play in the US Open, where she was represented by Roy Cohn, and notes her current support for bans on trans athletes in women's sports.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England winger Feyi-Waboso on track for Nations Championship after hamstring tweak
content:
England’s game-breaking winger Manny Feyi-Waboso is on track to be fit for international duty next month, despite tweaking a hamstring during Exeter’s match against Newcastle on Sunday. Initial scans have not revealed any major damage, leading Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter to express hope that the 23-year-old will return to action soon.

Medical staff from both Exeter and England have reviewed the player's scans, confirming that Feyi-Waboso will be unavailable for his club’s opening Champions Cup pool fixture at Toulouse on Saturday. Early indications remain positive, with the winger expected to feature in England’s opening Nations Championship Test against Australia on 8 November.
summary: Manny Feyi-Waboso is expected to be fit for England's opening Nations Championship Test against Australia on 8 November despite a hamstring injury. Initial scans showed no major damage, but he will miss Exeter's Champions Cup match at Toulouse.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Infantino faces grilling at Fifa council meeting over World Cup sell-off and Trump prize
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is set to face intense scrutiny from council members during a Thursday meeting at the organization’s headquarters in Zurich. The agenda includes his role in the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair, and the decision to award Donald Trump the inaugural FIFA peace prize. One attendee has predicted the discussions could be “explosive.”

This gathering marks Infantino’s first face-to-face encounter with his critics since he rejected repeated calls for an extraordinary general meeting of the council earlier in the summer. Those calls followed the emergence of the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals. Opponents are expected to press for an independent review during the session.
summary: Gianni Infantino will be questioned by Fifa council members regarding the aborted World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair, and the awarding of the inaugural Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump. The meeting is expected to be heated, with opponents pressing for an independent review of these controversial decisions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Peak District inn holds cricket memorabilia from Bradman and Australia
content:
Tucked away on a hillside in the Peak District, a local inn has accumulated a wealth of memorabilia and stories left behind by touring cricket teams. The article contrasts this historic setting with the modern travel habits of professional cricketers, who typically stay in chain hotels like the Crowne Plaza or Holiday Inn and spend their downtime playing golf.

Visitors can reach the area by taking a train to Grindleford, a station marked by homemade bunting along the platform fence that highlights books about trains during the national year of reading. The surrounding landscape features early morning rain and autumnal trees, with golden beech and rusty horse chestnut hues visible on the slopes of Padley Gorge and in the nearby valleys.
summary: A hotel in the Peak District is filled with memorabilia and stories left by touring cricket teams, including Don Bradman and Australia. The article contrasts this historic inn with modern hotel chains, describing the rural setting near Grindleford station.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Martínez Says Wilcox Failing as United Teammates Share Frustration
content:
Lisandro Martínez’s criticism of Manchester United director of football Jason Wilcox mirrors the broader dissatisfaction within the squad regarding recruitment and squad depth. The defender voiced his concerns following United’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday. While teammates widely support Martínez’s assessment that Wilcox is failing, his outburst is also viewed as an effort to facilitate his own transfer, as he is out of contract next summer and intends to leave the club.

The recent loss leaves Manchester United with only two wins for the season. The team had previously secured six points from their first six Premier League matches, a start that marks the club’s poorest league opening in 40 years.
summary: Lisandro Martínez criticized director of football Jason Wilcox after Manchester United's 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid, a view teammates say reflects general dressing room frustration. Martínez is out of contract next summer and plans to leave the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Brighton defender Pascal Struijk's red card overturned after VAR review
content: Brighton defender Pascal Struijk had a red card shown to him during a match against Sunderland, a decision that was later described as controversial. The incident occurred after a Video Assistant Referee (VAR) intervention led to the overturning of the initial decision.
summary: Pascal Struijk of Brighton was shown a red card in a match against Sunderland. The decision was later overturned following a VAR intervention.
author: BBC Sport

title: Supreme Court to Decide Scope of 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act
content:
The Supreme Court will examine the scope of the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) on Wednesday, assessing how this decades-old privacy law applies to modern digital tracking tools. The case has the potential to influence current and future litigation regarding consumer privacy protections.

The justices are considering whether the VPPA safeguards consumers who subscribe to any of a company’s products or only those specifically covered by the original statute. The ruling will clarify the reach of the law, which was originally designed to protect video rental records.
summary: The Supreme Court will examine whether the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act protects consumers who subscribe to any of a company's products or only specific ones. The case could shape current and future lawsuits over digital tracking tools.
author: The Hill

title: GOP senators criticize Trump's deal to import Russian diesel
content: At least eight Senate Republicans have voiced public concerns over a surprise agreement between President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to import 2.2 million tons of Russian diesel into the U.S. market. The deal would facilitate the importation of hundreds of thousands of tons of fuel, a move that has drawn criticism from a growing number of GOP senators.
summary: At least eight Republican senators have expressed public concerns over President Trump's surprise agreement with Vladimir Putin. The deal would allow the United States to import 2.2 million tons of Russian diesel.
author: The Hill

title: Trump rejects OSCE election monitors, ending 2-decade tradition
content:
President Trump has broken a tradition spanning more than two decades by refusing to welcome international election observers to monitor the upcoming midterm election. This decision has drawn criticism for discouraging democratic transparency.

Historically, the United States has routinely invited election observers from the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to observe and report on both midterm and presidential contests.
summary: President Trump is breaking a more than two-decade-long tradition of welcoming international election observers to monitor the midterm contest. This decision has drawn criticism for discouraging democratic transparency, as the U.S. has routinely invited OSCE observers to report on elections.
author: The Hill

title: School Start Times Scrutinized Amid Permanent Daylight Saving Debate
content:
School start times have taken center stage in the fight surrounding permanent daylight saving time.

Senators concerned about kids walking to school in the dark are holding the line against legislation — passed by the House and vocally backed by President Trump — that would halt the semiannual clock-changing. And while those who want permanent…
summary: School start times are under scrutiny in the debate over permanent daylight saving time. Senators concerned about kids walking to school in the dark oppose House‑passed legislation backed by President Trump that would halt the semiannual clock-changing.
author: The Hill

title: Three Bipartisan Anti-Fraud Bills Await Senate Action in Lame Duck Session
content:
Congress can make real progress on preventing fraud during the upcoming lame‑duck session.  

The federal government’s annual deficit has climbed to $2 trillion in 2026, underscoring the urgency of addressing waste and abuse.  

Three bipartisan House‑passed anti‑fraud bills are now awaiting Senate action. The bills remain in the legislative pipeline as the Senate moves through its final session before the new Congress convenes.
summary: The federal government's annual deficit reached $2 trillion in 2026. Three bipartisan House-passed anti-fraud bills are awaiting Senate action during the lame duck session.
author: The Hill

title: Sanctuary city whack-a-mole: Same policy, different ZIP code
content:
Sanctuary city whack‑a‑mole: Same policy, different ZIP code

The article highlights concerns about how sanctuary city policies may affect the principle of equal justice under law. It argues that the government should not discriminate against citizens in favor of illegal immigrants.
summary: The article argues that equal justice under law is compromised when the government discriminates against citizens in favor of illegal immigrants. It points out a whack-a-mole effect in sanctuary city policies, applying the same policy to different ZIP codes.
author: The Hill

title: Paul Clement, Republican former Bush solicitor general, challenges Trump policies in Supreme Court
content:
Paul Clement, a Republican, is preparing for his latest argument before the U.S. Supreme Court.  

Clement has accumulated dozens of wins at the Court since his tenure as George W. Bush’s solicitor general.  He is now challenging some Trump administration policies in the upcoming case.
summary: Paul Clement, a Republican, has secured dozens of wins at the Supreme Court since his time as George W. Bush's solicitor general. He has recently been challenging policies of the Trump administration.
author: NPR Politics

title: Kansas Senate Race Could Send Democrat to Senate for First Time in Nearly a Century
content:
In Kansas, a newly competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies

Kansas voters face a Senate contest that could elect a Democrat for the first time in nearly a century. The race also could flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even as the GOP confronts a potentially tough election year.  

The outcome would mark a significant shift in the state's federal representation and state leadership.
summary: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century. The race could also flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in a tough year for the GOP.
author: NPR Politics

title: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to midterm polling places
content:
Civil rights advocates announced plans to dispatch thousands of observers to polling places for the upcoming midterm elections.  

The move builds on a longstanding practice in which civil‑rights groups and political parties have sent monitors to voting sites, but organizers say the charged midterm environment has prompted many organizations to step up their efforts this year.
summary: Civil rights groups intend to deploy thousands of observers to monitor polling places in the upcoming midterm elections. The charged midterm environment is prompting many organizations to step up their monitoring efforts this year.
author: NPR Politics

title: Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns as U.S. ambassador to Greece amid misconduct allegations
content:
The White House publicly requested the resignation of U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle on Tuesday. The request followed mounting accusations of improper conduct against the ambassador.

Guilfoyle’s resignation comes amid reports that she faced a growing number of allegations related to her conduct while serving in the post.
summary: The White House publicly requested U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday. She faced mounting accusations of improper conduct.
author: NPR Politics

title: Chris Mason: Lib Dems rally behind Davey as he pledges change
content:
The Liberal Democrats are rallying behind their leader, Davey, following a series of resignations from the party’s frontbench. BBC political editor Chris Mason reports on the political fallout and the internal dynamics surrounding these departures.

In the wake of the resignations, Davey has pledged to implement change within the party. Mason’s analysis focuses on how the Lib Dem leadership is responding to the challenges posed by the loss of senior figures and the subsequent push for reform.

title: Ask HN: Will Senior Engineers Become Obsolete as LLMs Advance?
content:

The author suggests that companies like Anthropic and OpenAI could soon build datasets for software architecture, potentially making human guidance obsolete.

The post posits that business-wise, the need for actual software programming skills may decrease by 90% within a few years. It predicts that roles requiring people skills, such as product leads, will become more favored as agents handle the technical implementation. The author expresses skepticism toward the common industry assertion that humans will still be necessary for guiding agents and designing architecture, viewing the current era of human-driven coding as a "good run" that is coming to an end.
summary: The poster asks when the need for a human in the design loop will cease as LLMs become fully capable, and what currently stops LLMs from building datasets of good and bad architecture and RL‑ing that. title: Nonprofit Opens Free 3D Digital Leonardo da Vinci Museum
content:
The founder of a small nonprofit has launched Museum of Ages, a digital Leonardo da Vinci museum featuring a virtual tour with 17 stops. The free entrance includes close-to-real-size views of his paintings, 15 machines rebuilt in code, and 29 anatomy sheets. Visitors can also examine 207 selected manuscript pages in a virtual reading table, with 131 of those pages translated, and explore a reconstruction of da Vinci’s last house in Amboise.

The museum is available in seven languages and labels each stop with one of four grades: documented, reconstructed, conjectural, or not known. Detailed views allow users to inspect the sources for each element. The project utilizes Three.js for materials and runs on WebGPU, with WebGL2 as a fallback for unsupported browsers. Textures are derived from Creative Commons Zero photo scans and free 3D models.

The organization’s mission is to create walkable digital museums for individuals unable to visit physical locations due to illness, disability, cost, or distance. To ensure accessibility, the walk was pre-rendered to function on older phones and accommodate older users. The code is released under the AGPL-3.0 license, while texts and pictures are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
summary: The nonprofit Museum of Ages released a free virtual tour featuring 17 stops, including 15 rebuilt machines and 207 manuscript pages. The project uses WebGPU and Three.js to make museums accessible to people with disabilities or financial constraints.

title: General Assembly adopts pandemic prevention declaration with 153 votes, three against
content:
The United Nations General Assembly adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response on Monday. The resolution passed with 153 votes in favour, three votes against, and two abstentions.

The three countries that voted against the declaration were Argentina, Israel and the United States. New Zealand and Paraguay abstained from voting.
summary: The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response. The vote was 153 in favour, three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) and two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).

title: UN Special Representative urges stronger global action to protect children in crises
content:
The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children warned that global action to end violence against children is lagging behind the growing risks faced by boys and girls in crises. The representative called for stronger worldwide efforts to protect children caught up in an increasing number of emergencies.

According to the statement, current measures are insufficient, leaving many children vulnerable to violence as crises multiply. The UN expert urged the international community to intensify its response to safeguard children worldwide.
summary: The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children said current global efforts to protect children are insufficient. He called for stronger action to safeguard boys and girls affected by an increasing number of crises.

content:
Disasters cost $228 billion in housing losses every year, a figure that highlights the financial burden communities around the world face when rebuilding after a disaster strikes.  

The $228 billion represents the amount of money communities must find annually to replace damaged or destroyed homes. This figure underscores the scale of the challenge in restoring housing following natural or man‑made disasters.

content: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s two largest cities, Kharkiv and Kyiv, have again killed and injured civilians, damaging homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday. The attacks occurred in recent days, according to the OCHA statement.

content:
Secretary‑General António Guterres told the United Nations on Tuesday that “the need for the United Nations has never been greater” as the organization confronts climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger.

Guterres presented a programme budget proposal of $3.3 billion for the next year, which represents a reduction of $40.8 million from the previous level. The slimmer budget reflects the agency’s effort to align resources with the expanding challenges it faces.

content:

The IOM noted that despite the decline in the number of migrants attempting the crossing, the risks associated with the sea voyage remain unchanged.
summary: The UN migration agency (IOM) said fewer people from West Africa are reaching Europe by sea. It added that the journey has not become safer.

title: UNDP warns 800 million young people in developing economies risk unemployment
content:
The head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday that roughly 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies over the coming years will not find jobs unless countries act.

These initiatives are intended to address the projected employment gap for young people in developing economies.

content:
Canada‑born singer‑songwriter Joni Mitchell, 82, announced she has become a United States citizen. The milestone follows her move to the United States in the mid‑1960s.

Mitchell shared video of her naturalisation ceremony on Instagram, accompanied by a photo beside an American flag and the caption, “A journey that began 62 years ago.” The new status grants her the right to vote in U.S. elections, a privilege she previously said she was unable to exercise.
summary: Canada‑born singer‑songwriter Joni Mitchell, 82, posted Instagram footage of her U.S. citizenship ceremony. The ceremony, following her move to the United States in the mid‑1960s, now allows her to vote in U.S. elections.

content: A radio glitch triggered a false hijack alert, prompting German authorities to scramble fighter jets. title: Federal court overturns Tanya Plibersek's order blocking NSW goldmine
content:
A federal court has overturned a protection order issued by former environment minister Tanya Plibersek that had stalled the McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney in central‑west New South Wales. The order, which the company said effectively blocked the mine, was issued under section 10 of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act in 2024.

Regis Resources challenged the order, and the court ruled that the former minister’s decision was invalid. The ruling removes the legal barrier that had prevented the goldmine from proceeding.
summary: A federal court has overturned a protection order issued by former environment minister Tanya Plibersek under Indigenous heritage legislation. The order, issued in 2024, effectively blocked the McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney in New South Wales.

title: What Happens in the Brain When You Can't Stop Laughing
content:
People often wonder what happens in the brain when laughter becomes uncontrollable. The article invites readers to recall a recent experience of laughing so hard they could not stop.

It suggests that such laughter can occur even in situations where it may not have been expected or appropriate.
summary: The article asks readers to recall a recent instance of uncontrollable laughter. It suggests that this may have occurred in an inappropriate situation.

title: Study of 20,000 Nigerians Links Drug Use, Climate Change, Poverty
content:
A new study of 20,000 Nigerians explores the links between drug use, climate change, and poverty.  

The research examines how climate change—traditionally viewed as an environmental problem—affects people when their world becomes unstable. It looks at the psychological impact on those whose livelihoods, such as farming, herding, and family provision, become impossible.  

The study highlights the broader social and mental consequences of climate instability on communities.
summary: A study of 20,000 Nigerians examines how drug use, climate change, and poverty are interconnected. It looks at how climate instability undermines farming, herding, and family provision.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Norwegian Scientists Identify Abnormal Antibodies as Possible Cause of Childhood Cancer
content:
Scientists in Norway have identified a potential new mechanism that could explain the development of cancer in children.  

The research indicates that affected children appear to produce an unusual amount of aberrant antibodies targeting the building blocks of the DNA repair machinery. These antibodies attack a diverse set of hundreds of proteins that normally identify and correct damage or errors in the genome, potentially disrupting DNA repair processes.
summary: Scientists in Norway found evidence that children produce an unusual amount of aberrant antibodies targeting the proteins that make up the DNA repair machinery. These antibodies may disrupt the repair process and contribute to the development of cancer in children.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Finds Postmenopausal Ovaries Stay Biologically Active
content:
A new study has shown that ovaries remain biologically active long after menopause. Researchers at Northwestern University and the Buck Institute for Research on Aging examined ovaries from 28 women and found that the postmenopausal ovary is not defunct.

The ovaries continued to remodel with age, displaying increased inflammation and changes in tissue structure. These findings suggest that the organ remains functionally active decades after menopause.

The study also identified a molecular link between ovarian aging and cancer.
summary: Scientists at Northwestern University and the Buck Institute for Research on Aging studied ovaries from 28 women and found that postmenopausal ovaries remain biologically active and remodel with age, showing increased inflammation and tissue changes. The study also identified a molecular link between ovarian aging and cancer.
author: Medical Xpress

content:

Woldbye said that not building a third runway would be a “huge missed opportunity,” urging clarity from the government on the future of the expansion.

content:
Wild bobwhite quail were recently sighted in multiple coveys at the University of Tennessee’s Ames AgResearch and Education Center. The sightings mark an encouraging milestone in the center’s ongoing effort to restore habitat for the species.

The quail were observed at the historic bird‑dog field trial destination, indicating progress in the project’s habitat restoration goals.

title: 210‑million‑year‑old dinosaur from Zimbabwe reveals distinct prehistoric ecosystem
content:
A dinosaur fossil dated to 210 million years ago has been identified in Zimbabwe, offering new insight into Africa’s ancient ecosystems.  

Scientists say the find reveals a surprisingly distinct prehistoric environment in the region. The evidence points to ancient climate differences that may have isolated dinosaur populations across southern Africa, fostering unique species.  

The discovery challenges earlier assumptions about how these dinosaurs evolved and how their habitats were distributed.
summary: A newly identified 210‑million‑year‑old dinosaur from Zimbabwe is helping scientists uncover a surprisingly distinct prehistoric ecosystem. The discovery suggests that ancient climate differences may have separated dinosaur populations across southern Africa, leading to unique species that challenge previous assumptions about their evolution.
author: Science Daily

title: Hot planet 320 ly away shares host star chemistry, confirming formation theory
content:
Astronomers have discovered a scorching‑hot planet located 320 light‑years from Earth that shares a striking chemical similarity with its host star, confirming a long‑standing assumption about how planets form.

The finding provides the first direct evidence for that fundamental assumption and could enable scientists to predict the composition of distant rocky planets and to identify worlds with conditions favorable for life.
summary: Astronomers have discovered that a scorching-hot planet 320 light‑years away shares a striking chemical similarity with its host star. The finding provides the first direct evidence for a fundamental assumption about planet formation and could help scientists predict the makeup of distant rocky planets and identify worlds with conditions favorable for life.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds people see AI as less conscious than humans even when behavior matches
content:
A new study finds that people maintain a sharp distinction between human consciousness and artificial intelligence even when the two behave identically. Researchers observed that participants rated the most responsive AI as less conscious than the least responsive human participant.

When the same behaviors were evaluated using the term “awareness” instead of “consciousness,” respondents judged humans and AI much more similarly. The results suggest that the language used to describe mental states strongly influences how people perceive the consciousness of machines.
summary: The study found participants rated even the most responsive AI as less conscious than the least responsive human. When asked about “awareness,” participants judged humans and AI much more similarly.
author: Science Daily

title: AI uncovers hidden shortcut in CO2-to-fuel chemistry, revealing 10,000 reactions
content:
Scientists employing artificial intelligence have identified almost 10,000 chemical reactions that convert carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, exposing pathways that conventional models failed to capture. The AI‑driven analysis highlighted a previously hidden shortcut in the reaction network, markedly enhancing the accuracy of CO₂ conversion predictions.

Among the newly uncovered routes, a surprising hydrogen‑based reaction stood out, offering a potential blueprint for designing more efficient catalysts. Researchers say the findings could guide future efforts to develop catalytic processes that turn CO₂ into usable fuel.
summary: Scientists used artificial intelligence to identify nearly 10,000 chemical reactions that convert carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals. The finding improved CO2 conversion predictions and revealed a surprising hydrogen reaction that may guide more efficient catalysts.
author: Science Daily

title: New knee arthritis treatment provides lasting pain relief without surgery
content:
A new non‑surgical therapy for knee arthritis has shown the ability to provide lasting pain relief, according to a recent clinical study. The treatment employs tiny, dissolvable particles that block abnormal blood vessels in the knee, reducing inflammation and pain without the need for joint replacement surgery.

The study evaluated 194 patients who received the particle‑based injection. Eighty percent of participants reported clinically meaningful pain relief that persisted for at least 12 months after treatment. Researchers attribute the sustained benefit to the particles’ targeted action on the abnormal vasculature that contributes to arthritis symptoms.
summary: The treatment uses tiny, dissolvable particles to block abnormal blood vessels, reducing inflammation and pain without joint replacement surgery. In a study of 194 patients, 80% reported clinically meaningful pain relief lasting at least 12 months.

title: Prehistoric snake Vasuki indicus discovered in India could have been 50 ft long
content:
A massive prehistoric snake uncovered in India has been named Vasuki indicus and may have been one of the largest snakes ever known.  

The 47‑million‑year‑old fossil indicates the animal could have reached lengths of up to 50 feet, putting it on a scale comparable to the legendary Titanoboa.  

Scientists say the snake’s enormous body would have made it a slow‑moving ambush predator, a hunting style similar to that of modern anacondas.
summary: Scientists have identified a 47‑million‑year‑old snake named Vasuki indicus in India that could have reached up to 50 feet long. They believe its enormous body would have made it a slow‑moving ambush predator like a modern anaconda.

content:

The advance figures show gross domestic product expanding 5.4 percent in the third quarter. This performance highlights a robust period for Singapore’s output.

content:

content:

title: Championship roundup: racist chanting mars Swansea’s win at Millwall
content:
Substitute Ronald scored a last-minute winner to keep Swansea City top of the Championship, despite their match at Millwall being interrupted for nearly seven minutes. The delay occurred after a complaint was raised regarding racist chanting at the Den, prompting referee Edward Duckworth to halt play in the 65th minute.

During the suspension, Duckworth walked to the dugouts to speak with Millwall manager Alex Neil, Swansea counterpart Vítor Matos, and fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo. content: Bukayo Saka provided a significant response to a challenge set by Mikel Arteta by coming off the bench to alter the course of a Champions League match against Lille. The player's substitution proved to be a turning point in the contest, delivering a "huge impact" on the game's outcome.
summary: Bukayo Saka came off the bench to change the game against Lille in the Champions League. His performance was a response to a challenge set by Mikel Arteta.

title: Carney 1812 post references British-Canadian forces routing US
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney referenced a United States-British battle from 1812 in a post on the social platform X on Tuesday. The post included a photograph of a small sculpture that appears to be a British figure.

Carney noted that on this day in 1812, forces from the United Kingdom were victorious in the conflict.
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday made a reference to a 1812 U. S.-British battle in which forces from the United Kingdom were victorious.

title: Pennsylvania records sixth measles death amid worst outbreak in 35 years
content:
Pennsylvania recorded its sixth measles‑related death on Friday, marking the worst outbreak of the vaccine‑preventable disease the state has seen in 35 years. The outbreak has placed Pennsylvania at the center of U.S. measles cases.

title: Democracy Defenders Fund files Hatch Act complaint over search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
content:
A watchdog organization filed a Hatch Act complaint on Tuesday over the federal search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D‑Minn.) home. The complaint was submitted by the Democracy Defenders Fund.

The filing calls for an investigation of the Department of Homeland Security and its secretary, Markwayne Mullin; Attorney General Todd Blanche; the Justice Department; and Joseph Edlow, the director of the U.S. agency referenced in the complaint.
summary: A watchdog group, Democracy Defenders Fund, filed a Hatch Act complaint on Tuesday against several federal agencies after the search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) home. title: Ossoff commits to 6-year Senate term amid 2028 speculation
content:
Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) committed on Tuesday to serving a full six-year term in the Senate, explicitly stating he has “zero interest” in a White House campaign. This declaration comes amid speculation that the Georgia Democrat has been floated as a potential 2028 presidential candidate.

Ossoff made the pledge during a Tuesday debate while running for Senate reelection. When asked to confirm his commitment to staying in his current role, the senator responded, “Yes, I will.”
summary: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.), who has been floated as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, committed on Tuesday to serving a full Senate term as he reiterated “zero interest” in a White House campaign.

title: JAX researchers map endometriosis lesion microenvironment to reveal pain mechanisms
content:
People with endometriosis frequently report that their severe pelvic pain, intense period cramps, and other life-impacting symptoms are not taken seriously by doctors for years. New research from The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) aims to address this issue by providing a detailed map of the endometriosis lesion microenvironment.

The study identifies key cellular interactions within these lesions, offering new insights into the biological mechanisms behind the condition.
summary: Scientists at The Jackson Laboratory have created a detailed map of the endometriosis lesion microenvironment. This research aims to help address the years of struggle many people face in having their severe pelvic pain and other symptoms taken seriously by doctors.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Bigger data reveal second, third, and fourth switches controlling a gene
content: Genome-wide association studies, or GWAS, are now widely recognized as a standard tool for identifying genetic variants linked to complex traits. These studies have successfully identified loci associated with a range of conditions, including breast cancer, heart disease, and diabetes.
summary: A genome-wide association study, or GWAS, can help identify genetic variants associated with complex traits. Such studies have identified loci associated with breast cancer, heart disease, and diabetes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Disadvantaged children with intellectual disabilities face greater mental health difficulties, study finds
content: A new study led by researchers at University College London (UCL) indicates that children with intellectual disabilities experience heightened mental health difficulties when they come from disadvantaged backgrounds. The research highlights the intersection of socioeconomic disadvantage and intellectual disability as a factor in worsening mental health outcomes for these children.
summary: A new study led by UCL researchers found that children with intellectual disabilities experience greater mental health difficulties. This increased risk is specifically associated with children from a disadvantaged background.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Epstein-Barr virus hijacks cell repair processes to promote cancer
content:
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a common herpesvirus that infects most people at some point in their lives. The virus establishes a lifelong latent infection in its host, which is often asymptomatic but can also cause mild illnesses such as mononucleosis, a condition known as the "kissing disease" due to its transmission via saliva.

In rarer instances, EBV plays a critical role in the development of multiple sclerosis and is implicated in nearly 2% of all cancers.
summary: Epstein-Barr virus is a common herpesvirus that persists in hosts for life, often causing mild illnesses like mononucleosis. In rarer instances, the virus plays a critical role in multiple sclerosis and nearly 2% of all cancers.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experimental cataract lens treats glaucoma with time-release bimatoprost
content:
New clinical trial results indicate that an experimental cataract lens can also treat glaucoma. Researchers presented these findings at the annual meeting of the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO).

The artificial lenses feature small pads containing bimatoprost, a widely used glaucoma drug. This design allows the medication to be released gradually into the eye.
summary: New clinical trial results indicate that an experimental cataract lens can help treat glaucoma. The artificial lenses carry small pads of the glaucoma drug bimatoprost, which is released gradually into the eye.
author: Medical Xpress

title: CWU says Royal Mail losing 400 postal workers a week
content: The Communication Workers Union (CWU) has reported that Royal Mail is losing 400 postal workers per week. The union attributes this exodus to the implementation of a new delivery system, which it claims is failing to function properly in hundreds of offices.
summary: The CWU states that Royal Mail is losing 400 postal workers every week. The union claims this increase in departures follows the introduction of a new delivery system that is not working in hundreds of offices.
author: BBC Business

title: New computational model guides lighting design for aging eyes
content:
Researchers have developed a new computational model that accounts for the effects of aging on the human eye's ability to discriminate color. The model is designed to guide lighting designs that make it easier for older adults to perceive colors.

The approach also aims to preserve the expected appearance of colors for individuals with typical color vision.
summary: Researchers developed a computational model that accounts for how aging affects the eyes' ability to discriminate color. The model can guide lighting designs to help older adults perceive colors better while preserving appearance for those with typical vision.
author: Phys.org

title: Patterned X-rays map 3D chemical structures 43 times faster with fewer measurements
content:
Researchers at Bar-Ilan University and collaborating institutions have developed a new X-ray imaging technique designed to map the three-dimensional chemical composition of objects. This method addresses the challenge of determining an object's internal material structure in three dimensions, a task that is significantly more complex than standard internal imaging.

The new technique achieves a 43-fold increase in speed compared to conventional approaches. Additionally, it requires more than 97% less measurement data to produce the same chemical mapping results.
summary: Researchers at Bar-Ilan University and collaborating institutions developed a new X-ray imaging technique to map three-dimensional chemical composition. The method is 43 times faster than conventional approaches and uses more than 97% less measurement data.
author: Phys.org

title: Optical skyrmions control motion of magnetic skyrmions
content:
Magnetic skyrmions (MSks) are swirling patterns of magnetization that form inside certain magnetic materials. These structures behave like actual particles, characterized by a stable internal structure and distinct boundaries. Due to their extremely small size and the relatively low energy required to move them, MSks are considered promising information carriers for emerging technologies, including low-power memories and logic circuits.

A major goal in the field remains finding practical ways to control the motion of these magnetic skyrmions with high precision.
summary: Magnetic skyrmions are swirling magnetization patterns that act like particles and are promising for low-power information technologies. A major research goal is to find practical methods to control their motion with high precision.
author: Phys.org

title: Study links auditory precision to faster language pronunciation mastery
content: A new study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology indicates that individuals with high auditory precision, the ability to notice fine details in sound, are more effective language learners. The research finds that these individuals master the pronunciation of new languages faster and more accurately than other learners.
summary: A study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology found that people with high auditory precision master new language pronunciation faster and more accurately. This ability involves being better at noticing fine details in sound.
author: Phys.org

title: Isle of Wight fossil reveals Europe's first long-clawed megaraptoran dinosaur
content:
A UCL-led team has identified a new species of megaraptoran dinosaur from a fossil discovered on the Isle of Wight. Described in a paper published in the journal Royal Society Open Science, the animal is a long-clawed predator approximately the size of a large tiger.

This discovery marks the first time a member of the megaraptoran group, characterized as agile, two-legged carnivores, has been found in Europe.
summary: A UCL-led team discovered a new species of megaraptoran dinosaur from a fossil found on the Isle of Wight. This long-clawed predator, described in the journal Royal Society Open Science, is the first of its group to be identified in Europe.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists discover giant fungus Dianjunus rex in Chinese forests
content:
Scientists have identified a new fungal species named Dianjunus rex in the forests of Yunnan, China, marking a significant find in mycology. This "fungal giant" is distinguished by its vertical fruiting bodies, which can reach heights of up to 50 cm (20 inches) and weigh as much as 2.2 kg (4.9 pounds).

The discovery challenges existing understandings of fungal size, as Dianjunus rex is the largest known species within the phylum Ascomycota. The fungus possesses a unique lineage that dates back approximately 65 million years.
summary: Scientists have discovered a new fungal species named Dianjunus rex in the forests of Yunnan, China. This fungus produces vertical fruiting bodies up to 50 cm high and weighing 2.2 kg, making it the largest known within the phylum Ascomycota.
author: Phys.org

title: Ultrashort laser pulses measure Berry curvature in single-layer tungsten diselenide
content: Researchers at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the University of Regensburg have developed a new method to determine the Berry curvature of electrons using light. This quantum property, which describes specific geometric characteristics of electron states, has previously been difficult to access. The team utilized ultrashort laser pulses to perform these measurements on a single atomic layer of the semiconductor tungsten diselenide. The findings were recently published in the journal Nature Photonics.
summary: Researchers at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the University of Regensburg developed a method to determine the Berry curvature of electrons using ultrashort laser pulses. They measured this property in a single-atom-thick layer of tungsten diselenide, and the results were published in Nature Photonics.
author: Phys.org

title: Simple cleaning steps may reduce deadly fungal disease risk for Australian wild reptiles
content:
Spring has arrived in Australia, and with the warmer weather reptiles are moving throughout suburbs, parks and scrubland across the country.  

Snake catchers and wildlife caregivers are responding to calls for help as these animals become more active.  

Reptile enthusiasts, known as “herpers,” are heading outdoors in search of their next sighting.

title: Pulse Local: Mac budgeting app runs AI models locally
content:
Niz has launched Pulse Local, a budgeting application for Apple Silicon Macs that utilizes artificial intelligence models running entirely on the user's machine. The app operates in a local mode that requires no account, ensuring that the financial ledger and user queries remain on the device without transmitting analytics or crash logs. Users can import bank transactions via CSV files in any currency to access a budgeting assistant built on a fine-tuned Qwen3 0.6B model.

The application’s architecture relies on code rather than the AI model to perform financial calculations against the imported ledger. To verify accuracy, a separate 4B parameter checker model double-checks each monetary response; if the two models disagree, the app indicates uncertainty rather than providing a potentially incorrect answer. According to the developer, this verification process reduced the rate of wrong answers from approximately one in five to five in 494 across the last three tests.

Pulse Local is available for free, with an optional "Connected mode" called Sync Pass costing $29 per year to synchronize US bank accounts through Plaid. While the initial download requires approximately 2.9 GB of models and money answers take 12 to 14 seconds with the checker enabled, the app currently supports only English and Mac platforms. The developer has made the model weights available on Hugging Face and is seeking feedback on incorrect answers and unhandled questions, with Windows support planned for the future.
summary: Pulse Local is a free budgeting app for Mac Apple Silicon that processes spending queries using local AI models without sending data to external servers. The app uses a fine-tuned Qwen3 0.6B model to interpret questions, while a 4B checker model verifies financial answers to reduce errors.
author: Hacker News

title: Film 'Digger' Called Perfect Climate Movie Despite Universal Dislike
content:
The film Digger presents a deeply uncomfortable narrative that challenges audiences to examine the stories society tells itself regarding the distribution of economic and political power. The movie serves as a vehicle for confronting these uncomfortable truths about who holds influence in various contexts.

As a climate movie, Digger utilizes its narrative to force viewers to reflect on these power dynamics, offering a perspective that distinguishes it from other works in the genre.
summary: The film 'Digger' is described as a deeply uncomfortable climate movie that forces audiences to confront uncomfortable truths. It challenges viewers to examine the types of stories told regarding who holds economic and political power.

content: An OpenAI employee is alleged to have used a chatbot to assist in planting a covert recording device within the company’s offices. According to the source, the engineer’s interactions with the AI revealed efforts to set up the listening device days before it was discovered in a meeting room utilized by high-level executives.

title: Apple's chaotic HomeView ad resonates with parents
content:
Apple’s new advertisement for its HomeView smart display depicts a chaotic morning routine involving a family of five, featuring yelling, misplaced keys, and discarded eggshells. This fast-paced and unruly presentation contrasts sharply with Apple’s typical clean and orderly marketing style.

Despite the unconventional approach, the commercial has resonated with parents, particularly those with teenage children, who feel the ad accurately captures the stress of getting a household ready for the day. The source notes that the depiction of morning chaos, such as struggling to get a young child ready, aligns with the experiences of many families.
summary: Apple released a fast-paced commercial for its new HomeView smart display that depicts a chaotic family morning routine. The ad contrasts with Apple's typical clean aesthetic but has resonated with parents who feel seen by the depiction of morning stress.

content:
Disney has reportedly offered $20 million to acquire the technology of Character.AI, a chatbot company described as “scandal‑plagued.”  

The acquisition would bring into Disney the tech of one of the first chatbot makers that has been linked to a child suicide, according to the available information.
summary: Disney may acquire technology from Character.AI, a chatbot maker linked to a child suicide. The offer is $20 million.

title: ESA Targets Anbernic Handhelds as "Superfake" Piracy Enablers
content:
The European Software Association (ESA) has announced that it is targeting Anbernic emulation handhelds, labeling them as “superfake” piracy enablers.  

The announcement notes that the devices themselves are not the source of the problem. Instead, third‑party sellers routinely distribute ROM‑filled SD cards that enable piracy.  

ESA’s focus remains on the Anbernic brand, while the actual sale of piracy‑enabling hardware is carried out by independent third‑party vendors.
summary: ESA has targeted Anbernic handhelds as piracy enablers. Third‑party sellers, not Anbernic, routinely sell ROM‑filled SD cards.

content:

title: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman Criticizes AI Doomsday Warnings at TechCrunch Disrupt
content:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to address AI leaders who are issuing doomsday warnings.  

Feldman urged those warning about AI’s risks to “maybe stop talking,” arguing that the industry’s focus on potential dangers is drowning out its benefits.  

He made these remarks during the TechCrunch Disrupt event.
summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman told AI leaders at TechCrunch Disrupt to stop focusing on risks and instead highlight AI's potential benefits. He criticized the industry for drowning out the benefits with doomsday warnings.
author: TechCrunch

title: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts personal AI assistants will become household staples
content:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said the market is moving toward a future in which personal AI assistants are as common as household appliances.  

Feldman predicts these assistants will operate through a hybrid model, with some processing performed on local devices and additional functions handled in the cloud.  

He indicated that this shift could soon make personal AI assistants a standard feature in homes.
summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman says personal AI assistants will soon be as common as household appliances. He says they will operate partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

title: Science Corporation implants vision‑restoring chip in first Stargardt disease patient
content:
Science Corporation announced that it has implanted its vision‑restoring chip in its first patient with Stargardt disease. The milestone marks the company’s initial clinical deployment of the device, which is designed to restore sight for individuals affected by the retinal condition.

At TechCrunch Disrupt, Max Hodak, former president and co‑founder of Neuralink, detailed how his company’s work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain‑computer interface (BCI). Hodak explained that the collaboration with PRIMA is a key component of the broader BCI strategy being pursued.
summary: Science Corporation implanted its vision‑restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient. Max Hodak, former president and co‑founder of Neuralink, detailed his company's work with PRIMA at TechCrunch Disrupt as part of a novel brain‑computer interface effort.

title: OpenAI employee arrested after hidden recording device discovered in office
content:
OpenAI announced that it had discovered a hidden recording device in one of its offices. The San Francisco‑based AI company said the gadget was “sophisticated” and had been found during a routine security review.

The company referred the matter to the FBI and has reported that one of its employees has been arrested. In a statement issued on Tuesday, OpenAI explained that it used one of its own models to analyze the device and determine its origin.
summary: OpenAI found a hidden recording device in one of its offices and referred the case to the FBI. An employee was arrested following the discovery.

title: Ukrainian bombings of Yandex data centres linked to drop in pro‑Russian online content
content:
Ukrainian bombings of Russian data centres owned by Yandex have sparked claims among internet users that pro‑Russian and far‑right populist content on social media has sharply declined. The users attribute the reduction to the strikes cutting off Russian disinformation “bots.”  

The article examines this claim in this edition of Truth or Fake.
summary: Internet users say that after recent Ukrainian bombings of Russian Yandex data centres they noticed a sharp reduction in pro‑Russian and far‑right populist social media content. They suggest the reduction is a direct result of the strikes cutting off Russian disinformation bots, a claim examined in this edition of Truth or Fake.
author: France 24

title: French investigators chase hackers who seized supermarket cooling units
content:
French investigators on Tuesday were hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack that highlighted vulnerabilities of connected systems, with no group publicly claiming responsibility.

FRANCE 24’s Sharon Gaffney interviewed Marta Rybczynska, a cybersecurity expert at Ygreky, who said that basic measures such as regularly updating software or passwords are essential to prevent hacking attacks.

No group has claimed responsibility.
summary: French investigators are hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack. Cybersecurity expert Marta Rybczynska of Ygreky said basic measures such as regularly updating software or passwords are essential to prevent hacking attacks.
author: France 24

title: China expands auto production capacity in Europe, partnering with local firms
content:
China is shifting from exporting cars to establishing full auto‑industry ecosystems in Europe, building production capacity and strengthening partnerships with local companies.  

Philipp Seidel, an automotive expert at Arthur D. Little, told France 24 that while tariffs and quotas can buy time, EU carmakers must improve their own competitiveness and avoid becoming overly dependent on Chinese suppliers.  

The article also notes that the latest IMF global growth forecast includes a warning about rising debt.
summary: China has moved from exporting cars to establishing full automotive ecosystems and building production capacity in Europe while boosting partnerships with local companies. Automotive expert Philipp Seidel of Arthur D. Little told France 24 that EU carmakers must improve competitiveness and avoid excessive dependence on Chinese suppliers.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV has cancerous lung growth removed in 90‑minute surgery
content:
Pope Leo XIV underwent a 90‑minute lung operation on Tuesday, during which a cancerous growth was removed from his right lung, the Vatican said. The procedure was described as radical, with the lower lobe of the right lung removed to ensure complete removal of the tumor.

After the operation, the Pope “woke up normally,” according to the Vatican statement. A Vatican source added that further tests are being carried out to determine whether the cancer has spread.

The information was reported by Seema Gupta of France 24 from Rome.
summary: Pope Leo XIV underwent a 90‑minute operation on Tuesday in which a cancerous growth was removed from the lower lobe of his right lung. He woke up normally and the Vatican said further tests are being conducted to determine if the cancer has spread.
author: France 24

title: Arsenal 3-0 Lille, Atletico Madrid 2-0 Manchester United in Champions League

title: Russian missile hits Kyiv power plant, killing at least two, no warning from allies
content:

The attack occurred days after U.S. President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv. The incident has raised questions over efforts to halt strikes on critical infrastructure.
summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said a Russian ballistic missile struck a Kyiv power plant without advance warning from Western allies, killing at least two people and wounding around 20. The attack occurred days after US President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv, raising questions about efforts to halt strikes on critical infrastructure.

content:

The unrest was sparked by the shooting of a 27‑year‑old woman by police, prompting the road blockades and tyre fires that led officials to enforce the curfew.
summary: Mauritius has imposed a curfew after a night of unrest over a police shooting. Protesters blocked roads and burned tyres in response to the shooting of a 27-year-old woman.

summary: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, a former gang leader, was sentenced to a term of 40 years to life for the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur. The sentencing concludes a 30‑year search for justice and follows Davis’s own writings about the shooting.

content: US authorities arrested a Saudi national who works as an OpenAI engineer after a listening device was discovered in a meeting room. The individual was charged with allegedly planting the concealed surveillance device. The case remains under investigation by U.S. officials.
