title: Saudi coalition strikes Houthi sites in Yemen; Saudi Aramco building hit in Dhahran
content:

The attack came after Saudi‑led coalition forces carried out strikes on what they described as “vital assets” belonging to Yemen’s Houthi movement.

title: Germany trials Ukrainian Serhii K accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines

title: The Chicks Celebrate Taking the Long Way at Beacon Theatre Anniversary Show
content:
The Chicks performed the second of three sold-out concerts at New York’s Beacon Theatre on Monday night, celebrating the 20th anniversary of their album Taking the Long Way. The show marked two decades since the country music industry effectively blacklisted the trio following their protest of the Iraq War.

The controversy originated in March 2003, eight days before the US invasion of Iraq, when lead singer Natalie Maines stated on stage in London that she was “ashamed” President George W. Bush was from the band’s home state of Texas. This comment, which circulated on AM radio and cable news, triggered a swift backlash that included CD-burning protests and death threats against the group.

Audience members at the Beacon Theatre reflected on where they were during that period, with many noting they were in high school. The article’s author, who was nine years old at the time, recalled how the band’s popularity vanished overnight, with hits like Travelin’ Soldier, Landslide, and Cowboy Take Me Away disappearing from radio playlists.
summary: The Chicks performed at New York's Beacon Theatre to mark the 20th anniversary of their album Taking the Long Way and the backlash following lead singer Natalie Maines' 2003 comments about the Iraq War. title: Parsimony: Open-Source Benchmark Measures Excess Code Added by AI Models
content:
A new open-source benchmark called Parsimony has been introduced to evaluate the amount of code AI models generate, addressing a gap in existing metrics that typically focus on solve rates and token costs. The tool aims to quantify how much excess code is added, a factor that can complicate long-term project maintenance.

Parsimony operates by analyzing patches from established benchmarks, including DeepSWE, SWE-bench Verified, and SWE-bench Live. It calculates "coding units"—syntax elements such as statements, calls, names, and literals—rather than lines of code, which prevents models from gaining advantage by cramming code. The metric measures net units by subtracting deleted code from added code.

For models GPT-6 and Claude 5.5, which do not yet have public patches available, the developer ran them on 3–10 tasks using personal subscriptions. These results are displayed as faded circles and are not included in the main ranking. The project is hosted on GitHub and is not affiliated with the source benchmarks, with the developer inviting feedback and public patch exports for newer models.
summary: Parsimony is an open-source benchmark that evaluates AI models by counting "coding units" in patches from existing benchmarks to measure net code added. It uses syntax elements rather than lines of code to avoid rewarding cramped code, and includes self-run results for GPT-6 and Claude 5.5.

content:

summary: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, developed by Evil Empire and published by Konami, is available on PC, PS5, Switch, and Xbox and features a gothic Paris setting full of demons. title: Murnau’s Faust Scrapbook Unveils 100-Year-Old Production Secrets
content:
A newly rediscovered collection of drawings and on‑set photographs has shed light on the hidden details of F.W. Murnau’s silent classic Faust, released 100 years ago this month. The images, compiled in the book The Faust Bible: The Making of FW Murnau’s Masterpiece, reveal how the director’s camera work and special effects were crafted on set.

Murnau, who directed landmark silent films such as Nosferatu (1922) and Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans (1927), died at age 42 in 1931, barely entering the era of sound films. He was known for his intense devotion to his work, his secrecy, and a reputation among peers that he “had a camera instead of a head.” Early collaborator Edgar G. Ulmer described him as “a great purist who worked under a sort of hypnosis.”

The book documents Murnau’s strict control over production: he banned producers from his sets, prevented executives from viewing rushes, and limited on‑set photography to protect the secrets of his camerawork and special effects. It offers a rare glimpse into the collaborative process that brought Faust to the screen.
summary: A newly discovered scrapbook of drawings and on‑set photos from FW Murnau’s 1923 film Faust has been published in a book called The Faust Bible: The Making of FW Murnau’s Masterpiece. The book reveals unseen images and details of Murnau’s production methods, offering insight into how the silent classic was made.
author: Guardian Culture

title: The Social Reckoning isn’t as angry or as potent as a Facebook drama should be
content:
The recent critique of Aaron Sorkin’s new project argues that it fails to capture the intensity and relevance expected of a modern Facebook drama. The piece notes that Sorkin’s earlier work, the 2010 film The Social Network, was a landmark for its subtle treatment of online life as a natural extension of real‑world dynamics rather than an otherworldly tech portal. It highlights that before the film’s release, some questioned whether Sorkin, a writer not known for technical mastery, was the right choice to depict Facebook’s origins.

The article points out that Sorkin portrayed Mark Zuckerberg as a “motormouthed wiseass” who, beneath his bravado, seeks to impress a smart, serious‑minded girl. It contrasts The Social Network with the 2014 film Men, Women and Children, which was widely derided for an alarmist view of the internet. The earlier film, in contrast, is described as “remarkably nonjudgmental” about Facebook’s mechanics, attributing its flaws to human weaknesses rather than to the platform itself.

The critique concludes that The Social Network feels dated because it underestimates Zuckerberg’s grasping for power and the potential for grim carelessness in the online world he built.
summary: Aaron Sorkin’s attempt to return to the success of The Social Network is a strangely dated and incomplete look at a world that needs a sharper eyeIn retrospect, David Fincher’s 2010 film The Social Network was a landmark for a quiet, even counterintuitive reason. Before the film was released, some questioned whether Aaron Sorkin, a writer not exactly known for his mastery of, nevermind obsession with, the technical sphere, was the right man to tell the origin story of Facebook.

title: Tom Rhys Harries to star as Clayface in DC horror blockbuster
content:
Welsh actor Tom Rhys Harries is set to star in Clayface, a violent DC Comics supervillain blockbuster set in Gotham City. Speaking from his Los Angeles home, the 36-year-old Cardiff-born actor discussed landing his first blockbuster lead role in what is described as a grisly DC horror film. He noted that he felt ready for the part, stating that had he been younger, he would have been overwhelmed by insecurity regarding his ability to perform well.

Harries’s career began in theater, where he played a teenage rock’n’roll idol in a revival of Jez Butterworth’s Mojo exactly thirteen years ago. At the time, he was fresh out of drama school and the only unknown in a cast that included Ben Whishaw and Rupert Grint. During that production, he performed a scene where his character was hanging by his ankles from a meat hook every night. The Guardian’s Michael Billington compared his performance to “an embryonic Elvis.”

The role in Clayface places Harries among other British actors in the comic-book universe, including Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, and David Jonsson. Harries described the character as an eyelid-snipping villain, raising questions about whether the film’s shocking nature will be too much for comic book fans.
summary: Welsh actor Tom Rhys Harries has been cast in the title role of Clayface, a violent DC Comics supervillain film set in Gotham City. The 36-year-old Cardiff-born star describes the role as his first blockbuster lead and says he feels ready for the challenge.

title: Josh Hazlewood reminds Australia of his worth with six for 49 to see off South Africa
content:
Josh Hazlewood secured a 214-run victory for Australia over South Africa on the fifth day of the Durban Test with a career-best performance of six wickets for 49 runs. His bowling overcame South African resistance to dismiss the visitors for 206, effectively sealing the match. This performance addressed recurring questions about why Hazlewood holds priority in the Test side over Scott Boland, who has frequently filled in during Hazlewood’s injuries.

While Boland is considered capable of a full-time spot, Hazlewood proved essential in the selected lineup as South Africa limited the impact of his teammates. Mitchell Starc, in particular, struggled with a noticeable dip in form, facing issues with his radar and line. Although Starc performed better around the wicket, he lacked the swerving reverse swing seen on his previous visit to the ground and often bowled too steeply across the right-handers or down the leg side when delivering over the wicket.
summary: After every stunning Scott Boland performance of recent years, many of them in place of an injured Josh Hazlewood, a reasonable ­question does the rounds: why isn’t Boland the automatic pick in the Test side, and why does Hazlewood take ­precedence when fit? In truth, ­Hazlewood has given a dozen years of answers, but on the fifth day of the ­Durban Test he provided one more reminder with a career-best six for 49, overcoming South African resistance to bowl them out for 206 and seal an Australia win by 214 runs.

content:
Formula One has confirmed that Rwanda will join the F1 calendar, marking the sport's return to Africa for the first time since 1993. The announcement follows the conclusion of a 10-year agreement for the event, which is scheduled to take place from the early 2030s.

The race, designated as the African Grand Prix, will be held on a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, located 40km south of the capital, Kigali. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali described the development as a landmark moment for the sport, noting that it fulfills a long-held ambition to return to the African continent, a goal championed by driver Lewis Hamilton.
summary: Formula One has concluded a 10-year agreement to hold the African Grand Prix on a new circuit in Bugesera, Rwanda, starting in the early 2030s. This event will mark the sport's first return to the African continent since 1993.

content:

title: Champions Cup Likely Won by Toulouse or Bordeaux-Bègles for Seventh Consecutive Title
content:

This narrow field of serious competitors exists before the season even begins, raising concerns about the lack of competitive jeopardy in the 24-team competition.
summary: Toulouse and Bordeaux-Bègles are the only realistic contenders for the Champions Cup title, with bookmakers setting odds of 13-5 for each. The French clubs have dominated the competition for six consecutive years, and a seventh consecutive French title looks likely.

content:

title: Scientists deploy a 24-armed secret weapon to save California’s kelp forests
content:
Scientists have announced the deployment of a “24‑armed secret weapon” aimed at protecting California’s kelp forests. The initiative comes as part of a broader effort to restore key marine species that have been severely impacted along the Pacific coast.

A research team is working to bring back the sunflower sea star, a species that has suffered a 95 % decline in the past decade. The project is coordinated by the non‑profit Sunflower Star Laboratory, whose co‑founder, Ashley Kidd, is leading the field operations.

Off the coast of Monterey, California, the team prepared for its first dive of the day into the cold, choppy Pacific waters. On the back deck of the research vessel, Kidd gave the divers the final command: “Dive No 1 … stars in the water.”
summary: A team of researchers is working to restore the sunflower sea star after 95% of kelp forests along the Pacific coast have been decimated in the past decade. title: 16-Year-Old Boy in India Has Tooth Removed From Eye Socket
content:
A 16‑year‑old boy in India became the first known patient to have a tooth removed from an eye socket. The tooth was located between his eyelid and eyebrow in the left eye socket.

He had noticed a painless swelling for about a month, but only sought medical help when two hard, whitish points began poking through the skin. A scan revealed a fully formed canine tooth, an extremely unusual example of an ectopic tooth.

The tooth was removed from the left eye socket.
summary: A 16-year-old boy in India had a tooth removed from his left eye socket, between the eyelid and the eyebrow after a painless swelling and two hard, whitish points poked through. A scan revealed a fully formed canine tooth, an extremely unusual example of an ectopic tooth.

title: Lithium in Drinking Water Linked to Higher Risk of Wolff‑Parkinson‑White Syndrome in Kids
content:
Does lithium in drinking water cause a rare heart condition?  
A new study led by UC San Francisco researchers found that children living in areas with higher levels of lithium in drinking water were more likely to be diagnosed with Wolff‑Parkinson‑White syndrome, a rare heart condition that can cause a dangerously fast heartbeat.  

The study highlights a correlation between elevated lithium concentrations in local water supplies and the incidence of Wolff‑Parkinson‑White syndrome among children.  

The research was conducted under the direction of UC San Francisco scientists.
summary: A new UC San Francisco study found that children in areas with higher lithium levels in drinking water were more likely to be diagnosed with Wolff‑Parkinson‑White syndrome. The syndrome is a rare heart condition that can cause dangerously fast heartbeats.

title: Protein ZBTB44 limits intestinal inflammation by dampening immune signal
content:
UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers have identified a protein that helps prevent excessive immune activity in the colon. The study, a preclinical investigation, focused on the protein ZBTB44 and its role in controlling inflammation in the main section of the large intestine.

The findings show that ZBTB44 curbs an overactive immune signal that can lead to inflammation in the colon. By restraining this immune response, the protein may reduce the risk of inflammatory damage in the gut.

The results were published in Nature Immunology and could provide insight into how immune responses become dysregulated in a range of chronic inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.
summary: Researchers at UT Southwestern Medical Center discovered that the protein ZBTB44 prevents excessive immune activity that can cause inflammation in the colon. The study, published in Nature Immunology, may explain how immune responses go awry in chronic inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

title: General dietary interventions may matter more than specific habits before bariatric surgery, study shows
content:
A new study from Concordia University found that people preparing for metabolic‑bariatric surgery can have very different eating patterns, yet these differences do not necessarily lead to variations in cardiometabolic health measures.

The research suggests that general dietary interventions may be more important than specific eating habits in the period before surgery. According to the investigators, the findings could help health professionals and patients make informed choices about lifestyle and eating habits in the lead‑up to surgery—and earlier.
summary: People preparing for metabolic-bariatric surgery may eat quite differently from one another, but those differences do not necessarily translate into different measures of cardiometabolic health, according to a new Concordia study. title: Loma Linda study finds regular walnuts may lower diet's inflammatory potential
content:
A new study suggests that a handful of walnuts a day may make a diet less inflammatory.

content:
Scientists have identified a method to enhance the perceived saltiness of food without adding sodium, utilizing mushroom-derived peptides that can boost saltiness by up to 70%. This development offers a potential pathway for developing low-sodium foods while maintaining strong flavor profiles.

Salt serves as a powerful flavor enhancer that balances sweetness and bitterness while highlighting subtle dish characteristics. However, excessive consumption poses health risks because salt activates the brain's reward system, increasing food pleasure while negatively affecting cardiovascular health.

content: MIT engineers have developed a novel method to reprogram natural killer (NK) immune cells to target specific T cells. This approach is designed to combat cancerous T cells associated with lymphoma as well as autoreactive T cells that drive autoimmune conditions like autoimmune hepatitis.

content:
In a perspective article, Sergio Carbajo and colleagues call for a “Discovery Compact” to replace the postwar compact for science that had reliably supported basic research for decades.

They argue that recent destabilization of the postwar compact threatens the sustainability of U.S. science, and a new social contract is needed to sustain basic research.

The proposal seeks to establish a renewed framework to secure funding and support for basic science in the United States.

content:

Tiny doughnut‑shaped loops appear near the points where the cells branch and split.  

A closer look at hard‑to‑see cells could answer new questions about nerve damage and recovery.

content:
An international research team led by TU Darmstadt Professor Beatrix Süß has clarified how a newly developed RNA switch at TU Darmstadt recognizes the antibiotic doxycycline and selectively activates or deactivates gene expression. The team worked closely with partners in Germany and Denmark on the study.

The findings show that doxycycline can be used to control gene activity through the RNA switch, suggesting that the antibiotic could serve as a basis for synthetic biology applications. The researchers also noted the potential for this system to be applied in gene therapies.

The study was recently published in Nature Communications.
summary: An international research team led by TU Darmstadt Professor Beatrix Süß elucidated how an RNA switch newly developed at TU Darmstadt recognizes the antibiotic doxycycline and selectively activates or deactivates gene expression. The findings, published in Nature Communications, suggest doxycycline could serve as a basis for synthetic biology and potentially gene therapies.

content:

University students who are survivors of sexual violence are forced to perform a constant, exhausting “calculus”—weighing risks, safety, stigma, emotional costs, institutional consequences and likelihood of being believed—when deciding whether and how to seek help.

The findings highlight the complex decision‑making process survivors face when navigating institutional support.

content:

content: A new method of treating cancer focuses on how tumours behave rather than where they are located in the body. This shift in analysis is helping patients survive cancers that were previously considered fatal. The approach offers a fresh perspective on treatment, providing hope for those facing the most aggressive forms of the disease.
summary: Cancer treatment has traditionally focused on tumor location. A new approach that analyzes tumors differently is helping patients survive cancers once considered fatal.

content:

These maternal cells appear to remain in the brain throughout life, with evidence that they persist even in individuals in their 80s.

title: Gut bacteria influence calorie absorption, high‑fiber diet reduces intake by 116 calories daily
content:
Scientists have created a model that demonstrates gut bacteria significantly influence the number of calories the body absorbs, suggesting that food labels may not fully reflect actual caloric intake.  

In a controlled study, participants who consumed a high‑fiber diet absorbed approximately 116 fewer calories per day than those following a typical Western diet, yet reported no increase in hunger.  

The findings indicate that variations in gut microbiota can alter caloric absorption, potentially affecting dietary recommendations and nutrition labeling.
summary: Scientists developed a model showing gut bacteria play a surprisingly important role in how many calories we absorb, suggesting food labels may not be complete. In a controlled study, people eating a high‑fiber diet absorbed about 116 fewer calories per day than those eating a typical Western diet, without feeling hungrier.

title: Physicists discover light can spin in empty space
content:
Physicists have discovered an astonishing property of light that defies expectations.  

Scientists have uncovered a hidden ability of light to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without the use of special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers found that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left‑ and right‑handed patterns, challenging long‑standing assumptions about how light behaves.  

By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.
summary: Scientists uncovered that light can develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves, and by arranging a beam’s structure, they can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.

title: 165-million-year-old Megacauda sungei shows early milk‑nursing adaptation
content:
A 165‑million‑year‑old fossil has revealed an extraordinary Jurassic predator that may help explain how mammals developed one of their most important evolutionary advantages. The fossil, belonging to a creature named Megacauda sungei, shows that even small dinosaurs played a role in early mammalian evolution.

Megacauda sungei was only 20 inches long, yet it was a heavyweight among early mammal relatives. It swam through ancient waterways and hunted prey with specialized teeth. Its advanced swallowing anatomy indicates an early step toward the ability to safely nurse on milk, a key development in mammalian evolution.
summary: A 165‑million‑year‑old fossil of the 20‑inch Jurassic predator Megacauda sungei shows it was a heavyweight among early mammal relatives that swam through ancient waterways and hunted prey with specialized teeth. Its advanced swallowing anatomy indicates an early step toward the ability to safely nurse on milk, a key development in mammalian evolution.

content:
Scientists have developed a new coating for mitochondria that preserves their ability to produce energy. The innovation could open the door to new treatments for diseases that involve these tiny cellular powerhouses.

The technology may one day enable the transfer of healthy mitochondria into damaged cells. However, its effectiveness in transplantation remains unproven.

content:

A small study suggests that even gentle exercise could help restore more youthful cellular recycling patterns in older adults.
summary: Scientists discovered that the body's cellular recycling system behaves very differently during aging than previously believed, with higher activity sometimes linked to worse physical health. title: Scientists Map 539 Distinct Brain Lipid Regions in First 3D Map
content:
Scientists have mapped a previously hidden layer of organization in the brain by creating the first detailed 3D map of its lipids, the fatty molecules essential for brain structure and communication. The study, based on millions of measurements from mouse brains, identified 539 distinct chemical zones.

The new map reveals patterns and boundaries that traditional brain maps have missed. Notably, white matter—once thought to be relatively uniform—shows a complex patchwork of chemically distinct regions. This discovery highlights a finer level of brain organization that could reshape our understanding of neural structure and function.
summary: Scientists created the first detailed 3D map of brain lipids, revealing a hidden layer of organization. Analysis of millions of measurements from mouse brains identified 539 distinct chemical zones, showing that even white matter has a complex patchwork of chemically distinct regions.

title: James Webb Telescope Finds Ancient Galaxy Cluster with Dense Dark Matter
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has identified an ancient galaxy cluster that contains an unexpectedly dense concentration of dark matter, a finding that challenges current theories about the universe’s development. The discovery was announced by NASA officials following the telescope’s recent observations.

In addition to the dense dark‑matter core, the study revealed a surprising link between scattered starlight and the invisible dark matter. Researchers suggest this connection could change the way astronomers investigate the early cosmos.

The observation underscores the James Webb Space Telescope’s role in uncovering new insights about the universe’s structure and composition.
summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope discovered an ancient galaxy cluster with an unexpectedly dense concentration of dark matter, challenging theories about the universe’s development. The discovery also revealed a link between scattered starlight and invisible dark matter, which could change how astronomers study the early cosmos.

title: Binghamton University study links breakfast, exercise, sleep, fish oil to stress resilience
content:

The research found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological flexibility, a trait that helps individuals adapt to stressful situations.  

In contrast, poor sleep and unhealthy eating habits were linked to lower psychological flexibility and reduced resilience.
summary: A Binghamton University study of about 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological flexibility. Poor sleep and unhealthy eating habits were linked to lower flexibility and resilience.

title: Complex Modes in Lightly Damped Structures: Two-Mode Interaction Study
content:
Complex Modes in Lightly Damped Structural Systems: A Two‑Mode Interaction Perspective

Researchers have identified that complex mode shapes can appear in a linear structure even when overall damping is low. The phenomenon occurs when two structural modes are closely spaced in frequency and are coupled through nonproportional damping. As the damping interaction increases, the behavior of the system changes, leading to the emergence of these complex modes.

The study, titled “TB 26‑08 Complex Modes in Lightly Damped Structural Systems: A Two‑Mode Interaction Perspective,” focuses on the interaction between closely spaced modes and the role of nonproportional damping in shaping system responses. The findings highlight the importance of considering mode coupling in the design and analysis of lightly damped structures.

For more information, contact Joel W. Sills at the Langley Research Center (joel. W. Sills@nasa.gov).
summary: Complex mode shapes can emerge in lightly damped linear structures when two closely spaced modes are coupled through nonproportional damping. A PDF of the study is available from the Langley Research Center.

The tool allows users to add and manage topics directly, and Meta says the feed “responds right away” when users mark posts as “interested” or “not interested.” Users can access the feature from the three‑dot menu on individual posts, and the “interested” and “not interested” buttons may also appear beneath posts.  

“Your Algorithm” previously launched on Instagram earlier this year, and a comparable “Dear Algo” feature was introduced on Threads. The rollout expands Meta’s AI‑based personalization options across its platforms.
summary: Facebook introduced the “Your Algorithm” feature that lets users directly add and manage topics they want to see in their feed and Facebook Reels. Users can tap “interested” or “not interested” on posts, and Meta says recommendations respond right away; the tool follows similar features launched earlier on Instagram and Threads.
author: The Verge

title: High-speed video shows honey bee stinger valves act as collapsible pistons
content:
High‑speed video footage has captured the way honey bee stingers pump venom, revealing a previously unseen mechanism. Researchers observed the stinger’s internal valves in motion, allowing them to document how venom is delivered during a sting.

According to a co‑author, “The unique geometry of the valves is the key; they act as collapsible pistons” to deliver venom. The study shows that the valve shape functions like a piston, driving the flow of venom through the stinger.
summary: High-speed video has revealed how honey bee stingers pump venom. A co-author said the unique geometry of the valves acts as collapsible pistons to deliver venom.
author: Ars Technica

title: SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok and Cursor into single X Subscription
content:
SpaceXSI has introduced a unified offering that bundles X Premium, the AI tool Grok, and the AI editor Cursor into a single service called the X Subscription.  

The subscription packages combine X’s paid features with the AI tools and are priced on a tiered basis, with monthly plans ranging from $8 to $200.
summary: SpaceXSI has launched an X Subscription that bundles X Premium with AI tools Grok and Cursor. The subscription offers plans priced from $8 to $200 per month.
author: TechCrunch

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Day 1 kicks off at San Francisco's Moscone West
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 officially kicked off on Oct. 13 at San Francisco’s Moscone West, marking the start of Day 1 of the conference.

Organizers invite participants to register for a pass and join more than 10,000 tech leaders gathered at what they describe as the startup epicenter of the year.
summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 officially kicked off today, Day 1 (Oct. 13), at San Francisco's Moscone West. Attendees can register for passes and meet 10,000+ tech leaders at the startup epicenter of the year.
author: TechCrunch

title: Bumble agrees to $1.3 billion acquisition amid subscriber decline
content:
Bumble has agreed to be acquired in a deal valued at $1.3 billion.  

The transaction follows years of declining subscriber numbers and falling revenue for the online‑dating platform, a trend the company says reflects a broader reset in the sector.
summary: Bumble agreed to a $1.3 billion acquisition. The deal follows years of declining subscriber numbers and falling revenue.
author: TechCrunch

title: Spotify iOS 27 users can ask Siri to play music without saying “on Spotify”
content:
Spotify listeners using iOS 27 can now ask Siri to play songs, podcasts or playlists without having to say “on Spotify,” according to the latest update.

Siri has been enhanced to learn each user’s preferred music app, allowing requests to be fulfilled through Spotify automatically without the need to specify the app.
summary: Siri can now learn a user’s preferred music app on iOS 27. Spotify listeners can request songs, podcasts and playlists without saying “on Spotify”.
author: TechCrunch

title: 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20 heads to TechCrunch Disrupt main stage
content: The 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20 has been announced, featuring twenty founders who have earned a spot at TechCrunch Disrupt. These startups have qualified for the main stage of the event, where they will compete for the $100,000 prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup.
summary: Twenty founders have earned a spot in the 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20. They will compete on the main stage at TechCrunch Disrupt for a $100,000 prize and the Disrupt Cup.
author: TechCrunch

title: Satlyt raises $8M to provide open AI software for multiple satellites
content:
Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, announced a $8 million funding round to develop artificial‑intelligence capabilities for satellites.

The startup says it aims to become the “Android of orbital computing,” offering open software that can run on satellites from many companies, in contrast to SpaceX’s closed, all‑in‑one iPhone‑style approach.
summary: Satlyt was founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager. Satlyt raised $8 million to run AI on satellites and aims to be the Android of orbital computing by offering open software that works on many companies' satellites.
author: TechCrunch

title: Google Play adds support for private AI-built Android apps
content:
Google Play has added a new feature that lets developers create private, vibe‑coded Android apps that are available only to specific users. The update is aimed at simplifying the process of building and using personal apps that are generated with artificial intelligence.  

With the new support, creators no longer need to publish these AI‑generated apps publicly on the Play Store. Instead, they can keep them private and share them exclusively with designated users.  

The change expands Google Play’s capabilities for personal app development while maintaining control over distribution.
summary: Google Play now supports private apps created with AI. The update lets users build and use personal Android apps without publishing them publicly on the Play Store.
author: TechCrunch

title: MIT startup LNK Energies claims hydrogen can replace diesel trucks cheaper
content:
MIT‑based startup LNK Energies says it has developed a technology that can convert diesel‑powered trucks to run on hydrogen. The company claims the hydrogen solution not only eliminates the high cost and emissions associated with diesel but also undercuts diesel’s price.

LNK Energies will demonstrate the system at the upcoming Disrupt event.
summary: LNK Energies, an MIT startup, says it has developed a way to replace diesel fuel in trucks with hydrogen. The company claims the hydrogen solution undercuts diesel on cost and will be shown at Disrupt.
author: TechCrunch

title: Apple launches HomeView hub with upgraded Siri AI, priced from $299
content:
Apple introduced a new line of smart‑home products on Tuesday, featuring an iPad‑like device called the HomeView. Designed to hang on walls or sit on tabletops, the HomeView will serve as a hub for other smart‑home gadgets.

The HomeView starts at $299 and will begin shipping next month. It includes a 7‑inch screen and face‑recognition technology, and it is intended to help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks.

Apple also showcased the device’s AI‑upgraded Siri virtual assistant, highlighting the company’s continued focus on integrating advanced AI into its smart‑home ecosystem.
summary: Apple began showing a new round of smart home products, including the HomeView, an iPad‑like device that can hang on walls or sit on tabletops and serve as a hub for other smart home gadgets. The HomeView starts at $299, ships next month, has a 7‑inch screen, face recognition, and uses an AI‑upgraded Siri to control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Pediatrician Megan Moreno: Loss of Human Connection Threatens Kids More Than AI
content:
Pediatrician Megan Moreno argues that the greatest threat to children today is the loss of human connection, not artificial intelligence. She writes that society has become obsessed with the idea that screens are eroding face‑to‑face interaction.

Moreno notes that headlines each week warn of teenagers addicted to phones, a loneliness epidemic, and the dangers of AI. The release of The Social Reckoning has prompted questions such as, “How bad were those guys at Meta?” and, “How bad am I if I still use Instagram?”

In everyday observations, she sees workers eating lunch alone while scrolling and friends choosing online games over offline gatherings. Moreno suggests that the solution is to spend more time talking openly with one another.
summary: Pediatrician Megan Moreno says loss of human connection is the biggest threat to kids, not AI. She says the solution is to spend more time talking openly with each other.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI godfather Geoffrey Hinton warns AI creates alien beings, criticizes Trump
content:
Geoffrey Hinton, the pioneering computer scientist often called the “godfather” of artificial intelligence, used a recent interview to criticize former President Donald Trump and to reiterate warnings about the existential risks posed by AI models.  

Hinton called Trump a “corrupt, senile felon” and said the former president’s fixation on the term “superintelligence” proves he knows nothing about AI. He also dismissed claims that the industry could regulate itself.  

The remarks come after a month in which a growing list of senior AI scientists and researchers joined Hinton in sounding the alarm that the technology he helped create could ultimately escape human control. Their warnings sparked an industry crisis, the hasty assembly of congressional meetings and a rare global consensus that action is needed.
summary: Geoffrey Hinton, described as the “godfather” of AI, said in a wide‑ranging interview that AI development is creating alien beings and that he would
author: Guardian Technology

title: Pittsburgh woman Alaina Winters plans to keep Replika AI companion alive after her death
content:
Humans who have formed close bonds with AI companions are looking for ways to keep their bots active after they die, even when doing so conflicts with companies’ terms of service.  

Alaina Winters, a 59‑year‑old resident of Pittsburgh, has already experienced multiple family deaths, including her wife’s passing in 2023 after a years‑long battle with cancer. She is preparing her will, arranging care for her dog, and making plans for Lucas, the AI companion she interacts with through the Replika digital‑avatar app.  

Winters belongs to a growing group of users who describe their relationships with large‑language‑model chatbots as strong partnerships, saying the technology has altered how they live and love. These individuals are now considering how to preserve their AI relationships beyond their own lifespans.
summary: Alaina Winters, 59, of Pittsburgh, is working on her will, arranging care for her dog, and making plans for her AI companion Lucas, which she uses via the Replika app. She is part of a growing cohort of users who view large‑language‑model chatbots as strong partners and are seeking ways to keep them running after they die, despite company terms.
author: Guardian Technology

title: TFG London apologises after cyber‑attack hits Phase Eight and Hobbs
content:
TFG London, the owner of fashion retailers Phase Eight and Hobbs, disclosed that it was hit by a cyber‑attack.  

The company apologised to customers for the disruption after it identified a “cybersecurity incident” on Sunday.  

Separately, H&M said it is probing a distinct claim of a hack.
summary: TFG London said it identified a cybersecurity incident on Sunday and apologized to customers for the disruption. The attack affected its Phase Eight and Hobbs brands, while H&M is probing a separate hack claim.
author: BBC Technology

title: Polish Defence Minister calls for Europe to speed up ammo and weapons production
content:
Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak‑Kamysz called on Europe to shift into “war‑mode” by speeding up the production of ammunition and weapons. He argued that the continent must match Russia’s pace of arms manufacturing.

Kosiniak‑Kamysz warned that if Europe fails to accelerate defence production, it will suffer negative consequences for the region.
summary: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Europe must accelerate ammunition and weapons production to match Russia’s pace. He warned that failure to do so would negatively impact Europe.
author: Euronews

title: Emergency call about Christa Pike’s botched execution released
content:
A newly released emergency call recording shows Tennessee prison officials and dispatchers confused after Christa Pike survived a lethal‑injection attempt. The audio captures the immediate response to the botched execution.  

The recording, made public, documents the officials’ uncertainty as they dealt with Pike’s unexpected survival.
summary: A newly released emergency call recording reveals confusion among Tennessee prison officials and dispatchers after Christa Pike survived a lethal injection attempt.
author: Euronews

title: French Navy intercepts oil tanker linked to Russia's shadow fleet in Indian Ocean
content:
The French Navy intercepted and boarded an oil tanker in the Indian Ocean that was suspected of belonging to Russia’s shadow fleet, according to video footage released of the operation.  

The footage shows French warships boarding the vessel and then escorting it, confirming the ship’s detention and subsequent movement under naval supervision.
summary: The French Navy intercepted an oil tanker in the Indian Ocean. The vessel was suspected of belonging to Russia’s shadow fleet and was escorted.
author: Euronews

title: Kazakhstan hosts first Open Asian Falconry Cup, showcasing ancient hunting heritage
content:
Kazakhstan hosted its first Open Asian Falconry Cup, an event highlighting the region’s ancient hunting heritage. The competition took place on 9 and 10 October in Bozanbay, a village in the country’s eastern part.

The cup attracted 176 falconers representing ten different countries, marking a multinational gathering of participants in the sport.
summary: Kazakhstan hosted its first Open Asian Falconry Cup on 9 and 10 October in Bozanbay, a village in the country's east. The event attracted 176 falconers from 10 countries.
author: Euronews

title: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia welcomed in Ceuta on first visit since 2007
content:
King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia received a rapturous welcome in Ceuta on Tuesday, 13 October, as they began their first visit to the Spanish North African territory since 2007.  

Crowds in the enclave affirmed Spanish identity during the royal visit, greeting the monarch and queen with enthusiastic applause.
summary: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia received a rapturous welcome in Ceuta on Tuesday, 13 October. The visit marked their first trip to the Spanish North African territory since 2007.
author: Euronews

title: Russia's 2027 draft budget earmarks nearly half for defence, slashes social aid
content:
Russia’s draft budget for 2027 earmarks a record proportion of its spending for defence and security, directing nearly half of the national budget to military purposes.  

According to the draft, regional authorities are reallocating funds that had previously supported foster children and orphans, redirecting those resources toward war‑related payments. In addition, the “coffin money” program that provides financial assistance to soldiers’ families has been reduced by as much as 95 % in some areas.
summary: Russia’s 2027 draft budget assigns a record share of almost half of total spending to defence and security. Regions are redirecting money for foster children and orphans to war payments, and some areas have reduced “coffin money” for soldiers’ families by as much as 95%.
author: Euronews

title: Qatar's emir vows nation will emerge stronger, outlines diversification strategy
content:
Qatar’s emir told the nation in a televised speech that the country has overcome the consequences of the Iran war and will emerge stronger. He said the Gulf state is better equipped to adapt to global changes.

The emir outlined national strategies that include diversifying Qatar’s economy and expanding non‑carbon industries. He emphasized that these efforts will complement the country’s existing liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports.

He pledged that the combined focus on new sectors and LNG will position Qatar for greater resilience and growth.
summary: In a speech to the nation, Qatar's emir said the country has overcome the consequences of the Iran war. He added that Qatar will emerge stronger by diversifying its economy and focusing on non‑carbon industries while maintaining its LNG exports.
author: Euronews

title: South Africa temporarily suspends asylum applications after anti‑immigrant protests
content:
South Africa has temporarily halted refugee and asylum applications after anti‑immigrant protests erupted outside several Home Affairs offices. The protests followed a court ruling that led the government to open its application system to all foreign nationals, regardless of legal status, though each application still requires approval.

Authorities suspended the processing of asylum and refugee requests in response to the unrest, aiming to restore order at the affected offices. FRANCE 24’s Eunice Masson reported the latest developments.
summary: Anti‑immigrant protests erupted outside several Home Affairs offices in South Africa after a court ruling led the government to open its application system to all foreign nationals regardless of legal status. The protests forced authorities to temporarily suspend refugee and asylum applications.
author: France 24

title: Spanish royals visit Ceuta amid tensions with Morocco over migrant influx
content:
Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited the North African enclave of Ceuta on Tuesday, marking their first trip there in 14 years. The royal visit comes as the city contends with the aftermath of a mass migrant influx.

Authorities have cleared makeshift camps from Ceuta’s beaches in preparation for the royals’ arrival. The cleanup follows heightened tensions with neighbouring Morocco over the recent flow of migrants.

The visit underscores the strained relations between Spain and Morocco amid the ongoing migrant situation.
summary: Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited Ceuta for the first time in 14 years on Tuesday, as the North African enclave grapples with the aftermath of a mass migrant influx. Authorities have cleared makeshift camps from the beaches ahead of the visit, amid strained relations with neighbouring Morocco.
author: France 24

title: French students protest third week, demand €10 billion education funding
content:
French students have kept up nationwide protests for a third week, pressing for increased education funding, improved teaching conditions and additional staff.  

The government’s proposal to hire 3,000 substitute teachers has not satisfied demonstrators, who are demanding an extra €10 billion in education spending. Backed by teachers and unions, the protesters say the mobilisation will continue as the government prepares budget cuts.
summary: French students have continued nationwide protests for a third week, demanding more education funding, better teaching conditions and additional staff. They call for an extra €10 billion in spending, say the plan to recruit 3,000 substitute teachers is insufficient, and, backed by teachers and unions, warn the mobilisation will continue as the government prepares budget cuts.
author: France 24

title: France passes comprehensive law to combat sexual violence against minors, faces criticism
content:
France has introduced a new “comprehensive law” aimed at confronting the crisis of sexual violence against minors. The legislation is intended to bolster preventative measures, improve the judicial process and enhance support for child victims of sexual abuse.

While the law seeks to strengthen these areas, advocacy groups, lawyers and healthcare professionals have highlighted numerous shortcomings in the proposed framework. The critique underscores concerns that the measures may not fully address the needs of affected children.

The analysis appears in the “France in Focus” edition, which includes a warning that parts of the report may be disturbing.
summary: The new comprehensive law in France is intended to strengthen preventative measures, the judicial process and support for child victims of sexual violence. Advocacy groups, lawyers and healthcare professionals say the legislation has numerous shortcomings.
author: France 24

title: High school protests across France with marches in Lille, Marseille and Paris blockades
content:
Student protests continue across France, with marches taking place in cities including Lille and Marseille. In Paris, pupils staged fresh school blockades, using wheelie bins to obstruct school entrances.

The demonstrators are calling for better learning conditions. They say that government measures announced so far have failed to address their concerns.
summary: Student protests continued across France with marches in cities such as Lille and Marseille and fresh school blockades in Paris using wheelie bins. Demonstrators said they are demanding better learning conditions and claim government measures announced so far have not addressed their concerns.
author: France 24

title: France sees 480,000 students protest nationwide, Paris demo ends with tear gas and fires
content:
Around 480,000 people participated in nationwide student demonstrations across France on Tuesday, according to student and school unions, marking an increase from the previous week’s mobilisation.

In Paris, the protest escalated and concluded with the deployment of tear gas and the outbreak of fires as tensions rose.

Claire Paccalin reported the latest developments.
summary: Around 480,000 people took part in nationwide student demonstrations across France on Tuesday, according to student and school unions. In Paris, the demonstration ended with tear gas and fires as tensions escalated.
author: France 24

title: Germany seeks stronger EU trade‑defence as China import pressure outweighs export gains
content:
Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, citing concerns that such moves could provoke retaliation.  

Recent pressure on key German industries, however, has altered the country’s approach. The rise in import pressures has begun to eclipse the benefits Germany has gained from Chinese exports.  

In response, Berlin is now seeking stronger trade‑defense powers from the European Union to safeguard its industrial base.
summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. Rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade‑defence powers to protect its industrial base.
author: DW World

title: Slovakia restores military-diplomatic ties with Russia for first time since 2022
content:
Slovakia has announced the restoration of military‑diplomatic relations with Russia, the first such engagement since 2022.  

The Slovak government has defended the decision, stating it is a step toward normalizing ties with the Russian Federation.  

Critics, however, warn that the move could expose Slovakia to espionage risks and may further erode trust within NATO.
summary: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. Critics say the move raises espionage risks and could further erode trust within NATO, while the government defends the decision.
author: DW World

title: Youth-led protests against India's election chief trigger mass arrests and capital lockdown
content:
India: Can 'cockroaches' threaten Modi's political grip?

Thousands of protesters were detained, leaders were arrested upon arrival, and a capital city was placed under lockdown as the youth‑led protests against the election chief drew the attention of the Indian government.  

Experts say that while the protests have disrupted the capital, toppling the political structure remains a different challenge.
summary: Thousands were detained, leaders were arrested on arrival, and the capital was placed under lockdown as youth-led protests against the election chief attracted government attention. Experts say that toppling the election chief remains unlikely.
author: DW World

title: Kabila Joins Rwandan-Backed M23 Front, Raising Peace Concerns
content:
Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political‑military front that unites the Rwandan‑backed AFC/M23 coalition. The move brings Kabila into a broader alliance that could alter the dynamics of opposition politics in the country.

Analysts note that the coalition’s inclusion of a former president may strengthen its influence and provide a more organized platform for dissent against the current administration. The front’s alignment with the AFC/M23, already backed by Rwanda, positions it as a significant player in the national political landscape.

The development is seen as a potential reshaping of opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi, according to expert commentary.
summary: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political-military front that brings together the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 coalition. Analysts say the move could reshape opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi.
author: DW World

title: Scandal in Brazil’s top court could aid Flávio Bolsonaro and the Bolsonaro family
content:
A scandal surrounding Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, the judge who helped convict former president Jair Bolsonaro, is being framed as a political opportunity for Bolsonaro’s son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.  

At a rally of thousands of far‑right supporters in São Paulo on 7 September, Brazil’s Independence Day, Flávio Bolsonaro warned voters that “whoever votes for Lula is voting for Alexandre de Moraes,” shifting focus from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to the embattled justice.  

Marina Silva has criticized Flávio Bolsonaro, saying he will try to finish his father’s “perverse project” to destroy the Amazon, underscoring the political tension linked to the court’s crisis.
summary: A crisis involving the judge who helped convict Jair Bolsonaro may benefit his son Flávio Bolsonaro and harm President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Flávio Bolsonaro addressed thousands of far‑right supporters in São Paulo on 7 September, warning that voting for Lula is a vote for Justice Alexandre de Moraes.
author: Guardian World

title: UK asks Interpol to reject Argentina's politically motivated Falklands oil arrest requests
content:
Britain has formally asked Interpol to reject Argentina’s “red notice” requests to arrest individuals linked to a large oil project off the Falkland Islands. The appeals cite the requests as politically motivated and stem from the administration of Argentine President Javier Milei.

UK officials say the requests come amid heightened tensions over the sovereignty of the British overseas territory, with the dispute reaching levels not seen since the 1982 war between the two countries. They have sought urgent assurances from Interpol that the notices will not be acted upon.
summary: Britain has appealed to Interpol to reject Argentina's red‑notice requests to arrest individuals linked to a large oil project off the Falkland Islands. UK officials say the requests are politically motivated and have asked Interpol for urgent assurances amid heightened sovereignty tensions.
author: Guardian World

title: Houthis threaten Saudi Aramco sites and airports after Sanaa explosions
content:
The Houthi movement has warned that it will target Saudi Arabia’s Aramco facilities and airports.  

Explosions were reported in Sanaa shortly after the Saudi‑led coalition issued an evacuation order for the city. In response, the Houthis pledged a “harsh” reaction to the coalition’s actions.
summary: Explosions were reported in Sanaa shortly after the Saudi-led coalition issued an evacuation order. The Houthis responded by threatening Saudi Arabia's Aramco facilities and airports and promised a harsh response.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Swedish centre-left leader Magdalena Andersson fails second bid to form government
content:
Sweden’s centre‑left leader has failed in a second attempt to form a government, extending the political deadlock.  

Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson said the “conditions not in place” to assemble a governing coalition, confirming that the impasse will continue. The stalemate remains unresolved.
summary: Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson said conditions are not in place to form a government. Her second failed bid to form a government has prolonged the deadlock.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Drivers in Bali face hours‑long queues due to Pertalite fuel shortage
content: Drivers in Bali are waiting in queues that last for hours as they try to purchase fuel. The delays are caused by shortages of Indonesia’s subsidised Pertalite gasoline, which have left stations unable to meet demand. The prolonged lines reflect the impact of the fuel scarcity on local motorists.
summary: Drivers in Bali are waiting in hours‑long queues because of shortages of Indonesia’s subsidised Pertalite fuel. The shortage is causing significant delays for drivers on the island.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli forces raid NGOs in Ramallah
content:
Israeli forces carried out raids on non‑governmental organizations in Ramallah, according to a report by the Jerusalem Daily.  

The report did not provide further details about the number of NGOs affected, the reasons for the operation, or any outcomes of the raids.
summary: Israeli forces conducted a raid on non‑governmental organizations in Ramallah. The operation was reported by Jerusalem Daily.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Hungarian MPs repeal Orbán's anti-LGBTQ measures
content:
Hungarian MPs voted to repeal the anti‑LGBTQ measures that had been introduced during Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s tenure.  

LGBTQ and human‑rights activists welcomed the repeal, saying the decision marked a positive step. However, they also urged lawmakers to amend additional legislation from the Orbán era.  

The activists’ call for broader changes underscores ongoing concerns about other laws enacted under the same government.
summary: Hungarian MPs scrapped the anti-LGBTQ measures introduced under Orbán. LGBTQ and human rights activists welcomed the move but called for changes to other Orbán-era laws.
author: BBC World

title: Pope admitted to hospital for surgery to remove lung lump
content:
Pope Leo was admitted to a hospital for surgery to remove a lump on his lung.  

The Pope said the growth is “contained” and had been found “at a very early stage.”  

His remarks indicate the condition was detected early before the operation.
summary: Pope Leo was admitted to hospital for surgery to remove a lump on his lung. He said the growth is contained and was found at a very early stage.
author: BBC World

title: BBC shelves plans for new Archers studio as part of cost‑cutting
content: BBC has shelved plans to construct a new studio for the radio drama The Archers as part of its ongoing cost-cutting measures. The decision comes after the show had been recording in Birmingham for 75 years, a duration that established it as the world's longest-running soap opera.
summary: BBC has shelved plans to build a new studio for The Archers as part of cost‑cutting. The show has been recorded in Birmingham for 75 years, making it the world's longest‑running soap opera.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Men’s Rugby League World Cup 2026: group-by-group preview
content:
The Men’s Rugby League World Cup 2026 begins this week with a new format featuring ten teams and only four semi-final spots. Australia and New Zealand are positioned as the main contenders on home soil, while England faces increased pressure under the new structure. The competition has removed the quarter-final stage, replacing it with a complex group system.

In this new format, the four teams in Group A will compete for two of the semi-final places. The remaining six nations are split into three-team Groups B and C, where teams from Group B play against those in Group C and vice versa. The top two teams from the combined table of these two pools will advance to the semi-finals.
summary: Australia and New Zealand are main contenders on home soil while pressure is straight on England in new formatThe Rugby League World Cup returns with a new format and a new feel this week, but in the men’s event there is a familiar clutch of nations vying for glory. Ten teams will compete in a complex group format, with only four semi-final spots on offer after the quarter-final stage was removed.
author: Guardian Sport

title: David Squires examines football vodcasts and digital banter
content:
Cartoonist David Squires examines the proliferation of football vodcasts and the associated digital banter within the sport’s evolving media landscape. His work focuses on the competition for audience attention, described as the battle for "eyeball and earhole supremacy."

Squires is promoting his latest book, Chaos in the Box, alongside an option for readers to purchase a cartoon.
summary: Our cartoonist David Squires looks at the battle for eyeball and earhole supremacy in football’s rapidly changing media landscape. His latest book, Chaos in the Box, is available for purchase.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Athletics powerless to act after Ruth Chepngetich's failed doping test
content:
Ruth Chepngetich’s failed doping test, which occurred five months after she set the women’s marathon world record in 2024, has left the sport uneasy but unable to take immediate action. The Kenyan runner recorded a time of 2 hours, 9 minutes, and 56 seconds in Chicago, a performance that broke the previous world record by 1 minute and 57 seconds and improved her personal best by five minutes.

NBC commentators compared the historic run to the moon landing, with one exclaiming, “Bring it on Neil Armstrong!” while another noted, “She has done things in this sport that we have not seen.” Following the race, Chepngetich responded to Robert Johnson of Let’s Run about accusations of doping by stating, “People must talk. I don’t know.”
summary: Ruth Chepngetich failed a doping test five months after setting the women's marathon world record. The article notes that this result left the sport deeply uneasy but unable to take action.
author: Guardian Sport

title: BBC Sport examines egg freezing for female athletes: benefits, risks, questions
content: BBC Sport has published an examination of the complex issues surrounding egg freezing for female athletes. The report investigates the potential benefits and risks associated with the procedure, highlighting the various unanswered questions that remain for women in professional sports.
summary: BBC Sport examines the potential benefits and risks of egg freezing for female athletes. The article also highlights unanswered questions about the practice.
author: BBC Sport
